name: Application
apex: An HTML interface over database objects: a collection of pages linked by navigation menus, tabs, buttons or links, sharing one session state and one authentication scheme.
workflow: Developer runs the Create Application Wizard to declaratively assemble pages and navigation, then edits each page in Page Designer.

name: Source Location and Source Type
apex: Per-component attributes deciding where a region/item's data physically comes from (Location) and how it is queried (Type).
attributes: Type: Function Body returning SQL Query
workflow: Developer sets Source, Location then Source, Type in the Property Editor's Source group to point a region or item at data.
skip_for_web: Table/View, SQL Query and PL/SQL function-body types are Oracle-DB query mechanisms; a JS app substitutes its own fetch/ORM layer per source.

name: Dialog attributes (page)
apex: Sizing and behavior settings that appear once a page's Page Mode is Modal Dialog or Non-Modal Dialog: pixel Width, Height, Maximum Width, extra Attributes and CSS Classes, and Chained to queue multiple dialogs.
workflow: Developer sets Page Mode to a dialog type first, then fills these to size and style the popup before wiring a button to launch it.

name: Dialog Pages (Modal / Non-Modal)
apex: A page whose Page Mode renders it as an overlay instead of full navigation: Modal Dialog blocks interaction with the page behind it until closed; Non-Modal Dialog opens a separate popup the user can work alongside the parent page.
attributes: requires a Dialog Page template in the theme
Dialog Template (Theme Default / Modal Dialog / Wizard Modal Dialog)
workflow: Developer sets a page's Page Mode to Modal or Non-Modal Dialog at creation or in the Appearance group; APEX only offers this if the theme ships a Dialog Page template.

name: JavaScript group (page attributes)
apex: Three page-level slots for adding JavaScript without a separate file: File URLs to load, Function and Global Variable Declaration, and Execute When Page Loads, which runs after APEX's own generated JS.
workflow: Developer pastes JS directly into these fields to prototype page-specific behavior before promoting shared code into a real .js file.
skip_for_web: Inlining JS into a database field works around no per-page source file; a Next.js page is already its own file, so script lives there.

name: Page Attributes (overview)
apex: The properties of the page itself, not a region or item, edited by selecting the page name node; controls page name/title, header/footer text, navigation menus, page-level JS/CSS, error handling, and authorization scheme.
workflow: Developer selects the page name in the Rendering or Layout tab to load page-level (not component-level) attributes into the Property Editor.

name: Rejoin Sessions (page attribute)
apex: Security setting controlling whether a URL to this page without a session ID can attach to an existing session cookie instead of forcing a new unauthenticated session, i.e. deep-linking support traded against session-hijacking risk.
attributes: requires Embed In Frames = Allow from same origin or Deny
requires Session State Protection plus checksum for All Sessions
workflow: Developer sets this per page, default inherits the app-level setting, only when a page must work as a bookmarkable deep link without a session parameter.
skip_for_web: A cookie-vs-URL identity problem tied to APEX's session model; a JS app's auth session rides on a cookie or JWT, no URL session ID needed.

name: Warn on Unsaved Changes (page attribute)
apex: A Navigation-group toggle that, when On, warns a user with a browser confirm dialog before they navigate away from a page holding unsaved edits.
workflow: Developer turns this on for data-entry pages; APEX wires it via the apex.page.warnOnUnsavedChanges JS API automatically, no custom code needed.

name: Adding/Copying Regions, Items, Buttons
apex: The mechanics of building a page's tree: drag a type from the Gallery onto the Layout, or right-click a node in the Rendering tab to create a matching child (Region, Sub Region, Page Item, Button); copy via context menu, Ctrl+drag, or Copy to other Page.
attributes: Create Region / Create Sub Region / Create Page Item / Create Button (context menu)
Show Legacy... (Type attribute, deprecated component types)
workflow: Developer drags from the Gallery or right-clicks a tree node to add a child component, fills in its Property Editor attributes, then Saves.

name: Code Editor (Property Editor)
apex: A full-featured modal code editor for attributes needing large code blocks (SQL, PL/SQL, HTML, CSS, JavaScript), with syntax highlighting matched to what the attribute expects.
attributes: Save and Run Page (from inside editor)
APEX Assistant (AI chat, if Generative AI configured)
workflow: Developer clicks the Code Editor icon next to a long-form attribute (e.g. region Source) to open the modal editor instead of typing in the small inline field.
skip_for_web: A code-in-a-modal editor exists because APEX attributes are code strings stored in the DB; a component-based app keeps this logic in real source files.

name: Comment Out / Uncomment (page components)
apex: A context-menu toggle that excludes a component from runtime, shown with a strikethrough in the tree, without deleting it; implemented as a build option named Commented Out applied to that component.
attributes: Commented Out (build option, toggle in tree context menu)
workflow: Developer right-clicks a region, dynamic action or process and selects Comment Out to disable it at runtime while keeping its definition, then Uncomment to restore it.
skip_for_web: APEX needs a special toggle because deleting and recreating a DB-stored component is heavyweight; a JS codebase just comments the code out or feature-flags it.

name: Copy Page Wizard
apex: Duplicates a page, in the same app or a different one, letting the developer set a new page number/name, choose whether to copy public reports, pick a breadcrumb, remap the Navigation Menu entry, and remap templates when copying cross-application.
attributes: Create a page as a copy of: Page in this application / Page in another application
workflow: Developer opens Create then Copy Page, or Create Page as Copy, picks the source page, assigns new identity/number, and confirms navigation and template mapping before Finish.
skip_for_web: Template re-mapping on cross-app copy exists because APEX templates are separate DB objects per app; a JS monorepo's shared component library has no such step.

name: Create menu (Page Designer toolbar)
apex: The toolbar's plus-sign menu for starting something new from within a page: a Page, a copy of the current Page, a Breadcrumb Region, a Shared Component, a Page Group, a Developer Comment, or a Team Development Issue.
workflow: Developer clicks Create and picks the kind of object to add, launching that object's dedicated wizard or dialog.

name: Deleting Pages (single, multiple, range)
apex: Removing a page also deletes its associated tabs, breadcrumbs and list entries; single delete lives in the page's own Utilities menu, bulk or range delete lives in the application's Cross Page Utilities.
attributes: Confirm Page Delete / Permanently Delete Page
Cross Page Utilities: Delete Multiple Pages
Cross Page Utilities: Delete Pages by Range
workflow: Developer deletes one page from Page Designer's Utilities menu, or goes to the application's Utilities then Cross Page Utilities to multi-select or range-delete many pages at once.

name: Gallery (component palette)
apex: A palette of available region, item and button types shown in the central pane; a developer drags an entry onto the page or right-clicks it for an Add To menu of legal drop locations.
workflow: Developer drags a component type from the Gallery onto the desired spot in the Layout, or right-clicks it and picks an exact target location from Add To.

name: Help Tab (attribute help)
apex: Inline documentation pane that shows the description and available options for whichever Property Editor attribute is currently selected, updating live as selection changes.
workflow: Developer selects an attribute in the Property Editor then clicks Help to read what it does and which values are valid.

name: Layout Tab (visual canvas)
apex: A grid-based visual view of the current page showing where each region/item/button sits; supports drag-and-drop reposition/copy/move and a right-click context menu, but hides hidden items (unlike the Rendering tree).
attributes: Layout menu (Display from Here / Display from Page)
workflow: Developer drags Gallery components onto the Layout grid to place them, drags existing components to reposition, and can isolate one region with Display from Here.

name: Left Pane (Rendering / Dynamic Actions / Processing / Page Shared Components tabs)
apex: Tree view of everything on the current page in four tabs: Rendering (regions/items/buttons/processes in page order), Dynamic Actions (client-side behavior rules), Processing (server-side logic), Page Shared Components (shared objects used by this page).
workflow: Developer right-clicks a node to add a new component of that kind, drags nodes to reorder or reposition them, and clicks a node to load it into the Property Editor.

name: Locking and Unlocking a Page
apex: A per-page mutual-exclusion flag preventing two developers from editing the same page at once; a locked page is read-only to everyone except whoever locked it, and only unlocked or self-locked pages can be deleted.
attributes: Page Locked (by another user, with lock owner and comment)
workflow: Developer locks a page before a long edit to block collaborators from clashing changes, then unlocks it when done; the toolbar padlock icon shows current status and owner.
skip_for_web: Pessimistic whole-page locking compensates for one shared dev database with no branching; a JS codebase already gets this from git branches and PRs per file.

name: Page Designer (IDE)
apex: The full-featured IDE for building one application page: a three-pane window (Left Pane tree, Central Pane canvas, Right Pane Property Editor) plus a toolbar.
attributes: Two Pane Mode / Three Pane Mode
workflow: Developer opens a page into Page Designer, selects a component in the Left Pane or the Layout tab, then edits its attributes in the Property Editor on the right.

name: Page Designer Toolbar - navigation, lock, save
apex: Top toolbar controls for moving between pages and saving: Page Selector/Finder, Show Messages (jumps to the erroring attribute), a page lock indicator, Undo/Redo, and Save / Save and Run Page.
workflow: Developer jumps to a page via the Page Selector, watches the padlock for editing rights, and uses Save and Run Page to persist and preview.

name: Page Finder (Page Selector)
apex: A searchable page picker, opened from the Page Selector toolbar control, that lists All Pages or Recently Edited pages in the current application and supports free-text or regex search.
workflow: Developer clicks the Page Selector, searches or browses by recency, then clicks a result to jump into that page in Page Designer.

name: Page Search Tab
apex: An in-page find tool in the central pane that searches component names, actions and columns on the current page, with Match Case and Regular Expression options.
workflow: Developer types a term to locate a component by name across the current page's items/regions/columns rather than scrolling the tree.

name: Property Editor (attribute groups, filter, pin)
apex: The right-pane editor listing every attribute of the selected component, organized into named functional groups, with jump-to-group navigation and keyword filtering.
workflow: Developer selects a component, jumps to a group or filters by keyword, edits the value, and can pin a keyword to compare across components.

name: Quick Edit (runtime toolbar)
apex: A mode toggled from the runtime toolbar that lets a developer click any live component on the running page to jump straight to it in Page Designer, or open a Wrench icon to edit its Template Options live.
attributes: Quick Edit Mode (click a component to open it in Page Designer)
workflow: Developer clicks Quick Edit, then clicks the on-screen element they want to change, landing directly on that component's editor instead of hunting the tree.

name: Run Application / Run Page
apex: Controls that render the live application or a single page in a new browser tab/window, for previewing work without leaving the builder.
workflow: Developer clicks Run Page in Page Designer or the page list to preview that page live; Run Application launches the app's home page.

name: Runtime Developer Toolbar (overview)
apex: A toolbar at the bottom of a running page (when Availability, Status is Available with Developer Toolbar) giving developers quick jumps back into the builder and live diagnostics without leaving the rendered app.
attributes: Page XX link (jump to Page Designer)
Developer Toolbar Options (gear: Auto Hide, Show Icons Only, Display Position)
workflow: Developer runs a page, uses the bottom toolbar to inspect session state, toggle debug level, or click straight through to Page Designer for the component under the cursor.

name: Save and Run Page - Global Page and Modal Dialog behavior
apex: Save and Run Page's target depends on context: on a Global Page it reloads whatever page or open dialog is active, not the Global Page itself; on a Modal Dialog page it refreshes that dialog, or opens it fresh.
attributes: Save and Run Page button (green arrow)
workflow: Developer previewing a Global Page component hits Save and Run to see it reflected on whichever real page is open, since the Global Page never renders standalone.

name: Utilities menu (Page Designer toolbar)
apex: Toolbar menu of page-level housekeeping actions: delete the page, view its APEXlang export snapshot, run Advisor, manage caching, view edit History, view its Checksum, Export it, or toggle Show/Layout display options.
attributes: Show: Tooltips, Text Messages Picker, Layout View
Layout: Two Pane, Three Pane, Reset Layout
workflow: Developer opens Utilities for maintenance tasks that are not attribute edits: deleting, exporting, checking integrity, or changing how Page Designer itself displays.
skip_for_web: Advisor, Checksum and APEXlang View are Oracle-specific integrity/export tooling; a JS project relies on its linter/typechecker and version control instead of a page-level integrity checker.

name: Component Page Types - data entry, search and structure
apex: The rest of the Component page family: data-driven forms, searchable reports, and multi-page structures: Dashboard, Data Loading, Faceted Search, Form, Interactive Grid, Interactive Report, Master Detail, Search Page, Smart Filters, Unified Task List, Wizard, Workflow Console, Plug-in Page.
workflow: Developer picks one of these for live data entry, search/filter UX, or a guided multi-step flow; each type launches its own dedicated sub-wizard with type-specific steps.

name: Component Page Types - reports and displays
apex: Component pages add page-level functionality; the report/display family covers static or data-bound content pages: Blank Page, Calendar, Cards, Chart, Classic Report, Comments, Content Row, Map, Media List, Timeline, Tree.
workflow: Developer picks Component in the Create Page Wizard, then a type; remaining steps vary by type, e.g. Cards asks for a layout of Grid, Float, or Horizontal.

name: Create Page Wizard (entry point and categories)
apex: The wizard for adding a page, launched from the app home page or Page Designer's Create menu; the first choice is how to build it: Generative AI (natural-language prompt), Component (page-level functionality), Feature (app-level functionality), or Legacy (deprecated types).
attributes: Create Page as Copy (shortcut into Copy Page Wizard)
workflow: Developer clicks Create Page, picks a top-level category, then a specific page or feature type, and fills that type's own wizard steps.

name: Dashboard Page - per-chart configuration
apex: The Dashboard page type's own per-chart settings, repeated for up to four charts, whether created via the Create Application Wizard or the Create Page Wizard's Dashboard Layout starting templates.
workflow: Developer repeats the same small form per chart slot: a source table, which column labels each point, and which column/aggregation gives its value.

name: Feature Page Types
apex: Feature pages add whole-application capabilities rather than a single content page: Push Notifications, About Page, Access Control, Activity Reporting, Configuration Options, Email Reporting, Feedback, Login Page, Theme Style Selection.
workflow: Developer runs Create Page, Feature and picks one; each generates its own pre-built page(s), shared components, and sometimes new authorization schemes or navigation entries.
skip_for_web: Some of these exist because APEX has no external identity or UI-kit provider; Paddock already gets equivalents from Clerk and its own design system.

name: Global Page
apex: A special page, one per user interface, historically called Page 0, whose components render on every page of the application automatically; used for shared chrome like headers or footers, still filterable per-instance with Conditions.
attributes: only offered if the app has none yet
workflow: Developer creates one Global Page, adds regions/items/processes to it once, then relies on Conditions on those components to control which real pages actually show them.
skip_for_web: A Next.js app already has a shared layout file wrapping every page; a global-page database object gets APEX the same effect without a layout-component tree.

name: Interactive Report / Interactive Grid - self-service report tooling
apex: The two flagship report types: Interactive Report (searchable, sortable, downloadable, savable as Named or Private reports) and Interactive Grid (adds inline spreadsheet-style row editing); both give end users self-service layout control with no developer code.
attributes: Column Heading menu (sort, hide, control break, filter)
Row Actions on Grid: Add/Duplicate/Delete/Revert Row
workflow: Developer drops an Interactive Report or Grid over a table or query; end users personalize their own view (columns, filters, sort, saved reports) at runtime, no extra work.
skip_for_web: A full self-service report toolkit in one region type is a lot of surface area; a JS data-table usually ships a smaller slice by default.

name: Legacy Page Types
apex: Deprecated page types still supported for backward compatibility but not recommended for new work: Form on Local Procedure, Summary Page, Legacy Data Loading.
workflow: Developer only picks these when maintaining an old application; new pages should use the modern Component equivalents instead.
skip_for_web: Explicitly legacy even within APEX itself; not relevant to a greenfield design.

name: Login Page (Feature Page type)
apex: A pre-built Feature page (page alias LOGIN) auto-created with every application, wired with processes that call the APEX login API for credential verification and session registration.
attributes: Select a page type: Login Page
workflow: Developer either accepts the auto-generated Login page, or reruns Create Page, Feature, Login Page to regenerate or customize one, then hand-edits its UI and processing logic.
skip_for_web: Paddock uses Clerk for authentication; APEX's own login-page-plus-login-API pattern is redundant with a hosted auth provider that already renders sign-in UI.

name: Master Detail (page pattern)
apex: A wizard-generated one-to-many editing pattern joining two tables; the developer picks a layout describing how the master and detail regions relate on screen and across pages.
attributes: Stacked (single page, editable grids, click master row to load detail)
Side by Side (master list left, selected record plus detail right, modal edit)
Drill Down (two pages: report page then form plus detail page)
workflow: Developer picks Master Detail, selects the two tables/views and the foreign-key relationship, then chooses one of the three layouts; APEX generates both pages or regions wired together.

name: Page Groups
apex: A purely organizational grouping of pages, with no runtime effect, used to make a large application's page list easier to browse and manage; created and assigned outside Page Designer's normal component tree.
workflow: Developer creates a group under Utilities, Page Groups, then assigns each page to it there or via the page's own Identification, Page Group attribute; empty a group before deleting it.
skip_for_web: A cosmetic grouping tag on numbered pages compensates for APEX having no folder or route hierarchy; a Next.js app already organizes pages by file-system folders.

name: Authentication (Verifying User Identity)
apex: The process of establishing a user's identity, by password, certificate or secure key, before granting access to an application; pluggable via built-in or custom authentication schemes.
attributes: built-in methods (DB accounts, LDAP, social, etc.)
workflow: Developer selects and configures one Authentication Scheme per application in Shared Components; APEX runs it before serving any page.
skip_for_web: Paddock already has Clerk for auth; APEX's own authentication-scheme subsystem is redundant with an existing auth provider.

name: Authorization Scheme
apex: A named rule, built on the identity authentication establishes, that grants or denies access to an entire application, a page, or a specific region/item/button; distinct from Conditions, which only control display logic.
workflow: Developer defines an Authorization Scheme once, then sets it as any page or control's Authorization Scheme attribute to gate visibility or access by role/privilege.

name: Branching with Dialog Pages
apex: Rules for where a Branch can send a dialog page: to another dialog only if both share the same Page Mode, or the target has Chained on for nested/reused dialogs, or to a Normal page, which closes the dialog and navigates the underlying window.
attributes: Dialog to Dialog (same Page Mode, or Chained)
Dialog to Normal Page (closes dialog, navigates)
workflow: Developer chains a multi-step dialog wizard by branching dialog-to-dialog with Chained on, or ends the flow by branching to a Normal page.

name: Build Option (feature toggle)
apex: A named Include/Exclude switch attached to one or more components (regions, pages, processes); wizard-generated Feature pages are wrapped in one automatically so they can be toggled off or permanently deleted as a unit.
attributes: components associated with a Build Option
workflow: Developer flips a Feature's build option to Exclude to hide it without deleting anything, or removes its components first and then deletes the build option to remove it permanently.
skip_for_web: A DB-row feature flag with only Include/Exclude and manual cleanup; a JS app typically uses a real feature-flag service or a config boolean instead.

name: Cancel Dialog / Close Dialog (dialog page actions)
apex: The two built-in ways to end a dialog: a Cancel Dialog dynamic action (client-side, no submit) or a Close Dialog page process (submits first, and can return dialog page item values to the parent).
attributes: Dialog Closed (dynamic action event on parent, for refresh)
workflow: Developer wires a Cancel Dialog dynamic action to a Cancel button, and a Close Dialog process to a Save button that returns values to the parent, refreshed via Dialog Closed.
skip_for_web: A dialog page is a full APEX page rendered in an overlay, needing its own closure/cancel/return-value plumbing; a React modal is a component with props.

name: Condition (Conditional Rendering and Processing)
apex: A logic check attached to a region, item, button, tab, process, computation or validation that must evaluate true for that thing to render or run, evaluated during Show Page or Accept Page.
attributes: Current Page Is (NOT) In comma-delimited list
workflow: Developer picks a Condition Type on any component then fills the type-specific fields; APEX shows/hides or runs/skips it based on the true/false result each request.

name: Debug Mode (runtime toolbar)
apex: Per-request verbosity control for the page's processing log, from off through increasing trace levels, viewable afterward as a debug log.
workflow: Developer sets a debug level, reproduces the issue, then opens View Debug to read the step-by-step render/processing log.
skip_for_web: A leveled server-side processing log is an Oracle/PL-SQL debugging pattern; a Next.js app already has framework/browser dev tools and structured server logs for this.

name: Implicit Commit Points
apex: Fixed moments where APEX auto-commits the database transaction: after page render, before branching on submit, before re-rendering on validation failure, after each computation or item-value change, and after queuing mail.
workflow: Developer designs processes knowing a commit may already have happened at these points, so an earlier step of the same request cannot be rolled back later.
skip_for_web: Pure Oracle transaction-management detail tied to one DB session per request; a Next.js app manages its own transaction boundaries per API route or server action.

name: Page Processing Engine: Show Page / Accept Page
apex: APEX's two-phase engine: Show Page renders a requested page's regions/items/buttons into HTML; Accept Page runs on submit, saving posted values then running computations, validations, processes and branches in order.
workflow: Developer designs a page once; APEX automatically calls Show Page on a normal request and Accept Page on form submission, no manual routing needed.
skip_for_web: This two-phase render/submit cycle is a server-rendered-forms pattern; a JS app already separates initial render from a form handler (Server Action).

name: Page Processing Points (Pre-Rendering and Page Submission)
apex: The fixed named slots in a page's lifecycle where a developer attaches a Branch, Computation, Process or Validation: before rendering (Before Header/After Header/Before Regions) and on submit (After Submit, Validating, Processing, After Processing).
workflow: Developer right-clicks the specific lifecycle point in the Rendering or Processing tab and picks Create Branch/Computation/Process/Validation so the logic runs at exactly that moment.
skip_for_web: A fixed sequence of DB-transaction checkpoints tied to one HTTP cycle; a Next.js app expresses ordering with plain function calls, not named slots.

name: Friendly URL Syntax
apex: Path-style URL: https://host/ords/r/path_prefix/app_alias/page_alias?parameters, mirroring ordinary web app URL hierarchies instead of numeric ids.
workflow: Developer sets Application Alias in the app Definition and Page Alias in Page Designer's Identification group so URLs read as words, not numbers.

name: REQUEST (button-click intent)
apex: A special value set to the clicked button's name (or an explicit Request value) whenever a page is submitted, letting validations, processes and branches run only for one specific action.
workflow: Developer names each button distinctly, then conditions a process or branch on When Button Pressed or Request = Expression 1 so it fires only for that submit action.
skip_for_web: A shared global for detecting which button submitted a form works around one-form-per-page HTML posts; a JS app already knows which handler fired per button.

name: Session menu (runtime toolbar)
apex: Runtime toolbar menu exposing the live session: View Session State shows current values for the page's session-state items, Session Overrides lets a developer override values for their own session only.
workflow: Developer opens View Session State to confirm what value an item actually holds server-side while the page is running, without adding print statements.
skip_for_web: Session state is a server-persisted APEX construct; a JS app inspects state via browser devtools or its own debugger, not a bespoke session viewer.

name: Session State
apex: Server-side key-value store, keyed by a session ID, that persists item and page values across page requests because HTTP itself is stateless.
attributes: Session (logical construct distinct from a DB session)
workflow: Developer relies on APEX to auto-save submitted item values into session state and re-hydrate them on later renders; can also get/set state programmatically.
skip_for_web: The whole mechanism compensates for stateless server-rendered HTTP; a Next.js app already has client state, cookies/JWT or server actions for this.

name: URL Parameters (query string)
apex: Named query-string keys APEX recognizes on a page URL to carry session id, set item values, request a named action, or change render mode.
workflow: Developer builds links/buttons whose target URL sets these params to pass values or trigger behavior on the destination page.
skip_for_web: session, cs and clear-cache codes are internal to APEX's server-rendered session-state model; a JS app uses normal route/query params plus client state.

name: URL Syntax (Friendly vs f?p)
apex: APEX supports two URL schemes: modern path-based Friendly URLs, and legacy f?p syntax that encodes app id, page number and session id positionally.
workflow: Developer enables Friendly URLs on the Application Definition; f?p remains for backward compatibility and is generated when Friendly URLs is Off.
skip_for_web: f?p positional encoding is Oracle legacy; a Next.js app just uses normal App Router paths/query params, no equivalent needed.

name: Built-in Substitution Strings (system globals)
apex: A large fixed catalog of read-only global values (app/page/user/workspace identity, file paths, formats, URLs), each exposed identically as a bind variable, a PL/SQL V() call, a &NAME. string, and sometimes a #NAME# template token.
workflow: Developer drops these tokens into URLs, SQL, PL/SQL or templates wherever an app/page/user/environment value is needed, without writing lookup code.
skip_for_web: Each is a differently-spelled accessor for the same handful of request-scoped facts; a JS app gets these from one request/session/context object, not dozens of globals.

name: Dialog Template (Page Template Type: Dialog Page)
apex: A special page-template type providing the JS hooks for init, close and cancel that a dialog page's markup runs through; per-page Dialog attributes (Width/Height/etc.) are injected into the shared template via #DIALOG_*# substitution tokens.
workflow: Developer copies a Dialog Page template (Modal Dialog, Wizard Modal Dialog, or Drawer) into the theme if none exists; each dialog page's Dialog attributes flow into it via substitution tokens.
skip_for_web: Wiring dialog geometry through template substitution tokens works around templates being separate DB-stored markup; a React modal component just takes width/height as normal props.

name: Substitution Strings
apex: Token syntaxes replaced with a live value at render time: #NAME# for template placeholders, &ITEM. for session-state items, &COLUMN. for IG/Cards/Map columns, #COLUMN# for other report columns.
attributes: Format filters: HTML, ATTR, JS, RAW, STRIPHTML
workflow: Developer types these tokens directly into region source, titles, labels or any attribute marked substitution-aware; APEX replaces them during output, HTML-escaped by default unless a filter overrides it.
skip_for_web: String-token replacement inside server-rendered HTML strings; JSX expressions/template literals already interpolate values type-safely without a separate escaping-filter syntax.

name: Tabular-form Row Substitutions (APEX$ROW_*)
apex: Per-row placeholders available inside validations, processes or conditions on a tabular form or interactive grid: current row number, whether its selector checkbox is checked, and its Created/Updated/Deleted status.
workflow: Developer references &APEX$ROW_NUM. etc. inside a multi-row region's process or validation to act differently per row during one bulk save.
skip_for_web: Row-identity placeholders exist because a tabular form posts every row as one flat request; a JS data-table just iterates real row objects in memory.

name: Template Directives
apex: Bracket tokens {if/}, {case/}, {loop/} embedded in a template attribute's text that conditionally show text, branch on a value, or repeat text once per list item during rendering.
workflow: Developer types directive syntax straight into an HTML Expression or other template attribute; only attributes flagged in Page Designer help accept it.
skip_for_web: A bracket-token mini-language for conditionals/loops inside DB-stored strings; JSX/template literals already provide real if/map, so this workaround is unnecessary.

name: Templates (concept)
apex: Templates define the reusable markup for how pages, regions, items, buttons and other components display; APEX composes a page's HTML from a stack of templates plus substitutions.
workflow: Developer assigns a template to each component type and adjusts appearance via Template Options instead of hand-editing markup; can build custom reusable Template Components.
skip_for_web: APEX stores templates as DB rows rendered server-side with substitution tokens; a React/Next app's JSX components already are the templating layer.

name: With and Apply Directives (Template Component invocation)
apex: The with directive assigns named argument values which the paired apply directive then passes into a Template Component plug-in, like calling a reusable component with props.
workflow: Developer writes {with/} arg:=value lines then {apply COMPONENT_NAME/} to render a shared Template Component with those values; directives can nest inside the values.
skip_for_web: Directly analogous to passing props to a reusable component; a JS framework does this natively via component props, no template-string mechanism needed.

name: Branching with Buttons
apex: A branch (link to another page or URL) can be tied to a specific button so it only fires when that button was clicked; APEX evaluates branches at defined points in page processing (before processing, before computation, before validation, after processing).
workflow: Developer creates a page branch, associates it with a button, and picks the processing point at which APEX should consider it.
skip_for_web: This is Oracle's server-rendered multi-phase page-submit lifecycle; a JS app's button just calls a client function or API route with no separate branch-timing concept.

name: Button
apex: A clickable control that submits the page, redirects to a page/URL, runs a dynamic action, or opens a menu. Created from the Gallery's Buttons tab and dropped into a region or a named button position.
workflow: Developer opens the Gallery, Buttons tab, drags a button into the Layout tab (or a region's button position), names it, and sets its Action.

name: Button Actions (Behavior, Action)
apex: Determines what happens on click: submit the page (with REQUEST = button name), run Trigger Actions only, redirect to a page in this or another app, redirect to a URL, or defer entirely to a Dynamic Action.
attributes: Redirect to Page in this Application
Redirect to Page in a different Application (needs target app Deep Linking)
workflow: Developer sets Behavior, Action to Submit Page for forms, a Redirect option for navigation buttons, or Defined by Dynamic Action when client-side JS handles the click entirely.
skip_for_web: Submit Page's REQUEST value and server-side branch/process gating on :REQUEST is Oracle's postback model; a JS app wires an onClick handler directly to a client action or API call instead.

name: Button Confirmation Dialog
apex: Requires Confirmation shows a styled confirm dialog before the button's action runs; cancelling aborts the action. Message text supports substitutions.
workflow: Developer enables Requires Confirmation on a destructive button (e.g. Delete), writes the Message, and picks a Style so the dialog matches the action's severity.

name: Button Displayed as Menu
apex: Setting a button's Behavior, Type to Menu turns it into a dropdown: each Menu entry gets its own Label and Link (Type/Target), entries can be separators, hidden (Comment Out), or reordered.
workflow: Developer switches the button's Type to Menu, then right-clicks Menus in the Rendering tab to add entries, setting each entry's label and link target.

name: Button Name / REQUEST binding
apex: A Submit-type button's Name becomes the page's REQUEST value on submit, letting server-side processes, validations and branches run conditionally on :REQUEST (case-sensitive).
workflow: Developer names buttons distinctly (e.g. EDIT, DELETE) and writes PL/SQL or conditions like :REQUEST IN ('EDIT','DELETE') to branch behavior per button.
skip_for_web: A single-page-submit-then-inspect-REQUEST dispatch pattern is specific to Oracle's postback lifecycle; a JS app gives each button its own handler or API route instead.

name: Button Warn on Unsaved Changes
apex: Behavior-group flag controlling whether clicking this button triggers the page's unsaved-changes browser warning; Cancel/Delete/Apply-Changes buttons typically set Do Not Check.
attributes: Behavior, Warn on Unsaved Changes: Page Default
Behavior, Warn on Unsaved Changes: Do Not Check
workflow: Developer leaves Page Default on Save-type buttons and sets Do Not Check on Cancel/Delete buttons so leaving via them doesn't falsely warn the user.

name: Hiding or Disabling a Button
apex: A button is removed entirely by setting its Server-side Condition Type to Never; combined with the Show as Disabled switch it instead stays visible but greyed out and unclickable.
workflow: Developer sets Server-side Condition to Never to hide a button outright, or adds Show as Disabled to keep it visible as a disabled affordance.

name: Show Processing (button)
apex: A Behavior attribute (Submit Page buttons only) that greys out the page and shows a processing animation on click, preventing accidental double-submits during slow operations.
workflow: Developer enables Show Processing on submit buttons that trigger long-running server processing.

name: Trigger Action (button)
apex: Setting a button's Behavior, Type to Trigger Action attaches a dynamic action (e.g. Execute Server-side Code) directly beneath it in the component tree, without submitting the page or redirecting.
attributes: nested action, e.g. Execute Server-side Code
workflow: Developer sets Type to Trigger Action, then configures the auto-created action node's own attributes to define the click behavior declaratively.

name: Calendar (region type)
apex: Shows date-based records on Month/Week/Day/List views, built on the FullCalendar jQuery library; supports duration events (with an end date), drag-and-drop rescheduling, click-to-add/edit forms, external feeds (web service, Google Calendar), and PDF/iCal/CSV/XML export.
attributes: Attributes, Settings, End Date Column (for duration events)
workflow: Developer builds a region of Type Calendar over a table/SQL query, picks Display Column and Start Date Column, and enables extra views/drag-drop as needed.
skip_for_web: Drag-and-drop is only supported for local database sources, not external feeds; a JS calendar library has no such source-type restriction.

name: Calendar Attributes (two attribute sets)
apex: A calendar region exposes two Property Editor tabs: Region (the container: layout, appearance, security like any region) and Attributes (calendar-specific: template, date columns, views, links, drag-and-drop).
attributes: Attributes tab: Settings, Start Date Column
Attributes tab: Settings, Primary Key Column
workflow: Developer switches between the Region and Attributes tabs in the Property Editor depending on whether they're changing the container or the calendar's own behavior.

name: Calendar Create/Edit Links
apex: Settings that turn calendar cells/events into links to a create or edit page, passing the clicked date range or the event's primary key as target-page items.
workflow: Developer builds a Create Link passing the clicked date(s) to a create-page item, and an Edit Link passing the row's primary key to a form page.

name: Calendar Drag and Drop
apex: Lets end users reschedule or resize events by dragging them on the calendar; on drop, a developer-written PL/SQL block runs with the moved event's key and new dates bound in.
attributes: Settings, Primary Key Column (required to enable)
Settings, Drag and Drop PL/SQL Code
workflow: Developer sets a Primary Key Column, turns Drag and Drop on, and writes a PL/SQL UPDATE using the three bind variables to persist the new schedule.
skip_for_web: Persisting the drop via a server PL/SQL block keyed on Oracle bind variables is this stack's mutation path; a JS calendar library fires a client callback with the same id/new-start/new-end facts for an API call instead.

name: Calendar Initialization JavaScript Code
apex: An Advanced-group attribute holding a JS function that receives and can override the underlying FullCalendar options object (time slot range, week numbers, date formats, etc.) before the calendar renders.
workflow: Developer writes a function(pOptions){...; return pOptions;} to tweak FullCalendar behavior beyond what declarative calendar attributes expose.
skip_for_web: This hands configuration straight to the FullCalendar library instance; a JS app using FullCalendar directly just passes the same options object, no override indirection needed.

name: Calendar Source, Location
apex: Where a calendar's row data physically comes from: a local database table/query, a REST-Enabled SQL reference, a REST Data Source, a JSON Source, an Oracle Duality View, or built-in sample data.
workflow: Developer sets Source, Location before Source, Type; the remaining Source attributes shown depend on which Location is chosen.

name: Chart (region type)
apex: Visualizes data using Oracle JET Data Visualization components: area, bar, line, pie, box plot, bubble, combination, donut, funnel, gantt, polar, pyramid, radar, scatter, stock, status meter gauge and more, with animation and responsive layout built in.
attributes: Series node (one or more, per data series)
workflow: Developer adds a Chart region via wizard or Page Designer Gallery, then configures its Series (data) and, for applicable types, its Axes.

name: Chart Attribute Structure (Region/Attributes/Series)
apex: A chart exposes three attribute surfaces: Region (container), Attributes tab (chart-level settings including Chart, Type), and per-Series attributes nested under the chart in the Rendering tab.
attributes: Series (per data series, own Column Mapping/Type)
workflow: Developer switches chart type via Attributes tab, Chart, Type, then re-checks each Series' Column Mapping since required mappings differ per chart type.

name: Chart Automatic Refresh
apex: Keeps a chart current either by polling on a fixed interval (Automatic Refresh) or by firing a Dynamic Action's Refresh action on some other event (e.g. page load, a button click).
attributes: Dynamic Action: Execution, Fire on Initialization
workflow: Developer sets an Interval for simple polling, or builds a Refresh dynamic action targeting the chart's region when refresh should be event-driven instead of timed.

name: Chart Axes
apex: An Axes node (shown only for axis-based chart types: area, bar, bubble, combination, line, line with area, polar, radar, range, scatter, stock) exposing per-axis formatting attributes.
workflow: Developer expands Axes under the chart, selects an axis, and sets its formatting once the chart type supports axes.

name: Chart Creation Methods and Types
apex: Charts can be created via the Create Application Wizard (Area/Bar/Line/Pie, single chart or 4-chart dashboard), the Create Page Wizard (adds Box Plot, Bubble, Combination, Status Meter Gauge, Donut, Funnel, Gantt, Line with Area, Polar, Pyramid, Radar, Scatter, Stock), or manually in Page Designer.
attributes: Create Page Wizard: Chart / Dashboard (4 layout options)
workflow: Developer picks the Create Page Wizard for the widest chart-type selection, or adds a Chart region manually in Page Designer for full control.

name: Chart Custom JavaScript (JET options)
apex: An Advanced-group JS function that receives and can mutate the chart's Oracle JET options object directly (series colors, chart type, data filtering) before render.
workflow: Developer writes function(options){...; return options;} to reach JET chart options (ojChart) not exposed as declarative attributes.
skip_for_web: This passes options straight through to the underlying Oracle JET ojChart component; a JS charting library (the same JET, or Chart.js/ECharts) takes an equivalent options object natively.

name: Chart Series
apex: Each chart has one or more Series nodes defining one data set: where its rows come from (Source, Location) and which columns map to the chart's label/value axes.
attributes: Source, Location: Local Database/REST Enabled SQL/REST Source/Duality View/JSON Source/Sample Data
Type (Series Type, e.g. Bar Range) for Combination/Polar/Radar/Range charts
workflow: Developer expands the Series node under the chart in the Rendering tab, sets its Source, then maps the Label and Value columns.

name: Application Item
apex: A named session-state slot with no UI, not tied to any page: used as a global variable across pages, or (Scope=Global) shared across multiple applications on the same session.
attributes: Security, Session State Protection (Unrestricted / Restricted / Checksum Required: Application, User or Session Level)
workflow: Developer creates it under Shared Components > Application Items, sets Scope and Session State Protection, then sets its value via computation, process, or URL rather than direct user input.
skip_for_web: Session State Protection's checksum tiers guard Oracle's URL-based state-setting (f?p links); a JS app has no equivalent since state changes go through authenticated API calls, not signed URL parameters.

name: Checkbox (item type)
apex: A single tick box holding one of two stored values (checked/unchecked).
workflow: Developer either accepts app-level checkbox defaults (Component Settings) or turns Use Defaults off and sets Checked/Unchecked Value explicitly.

name: Checkbox Group (item type)
apex: Renders a List of Values as multiple checkboxes for multi-select; checked entries are stored as one colon-delimited string.
workflow: Developer attaches a LOV, sets Number of Columns for layout, and configures Multiple Values Type/Separator to control how the checked set is encoded.
skip_for_web: Colon-delimited-string encoding of a multi-select works around a single SQL column being scalar; a JS app stores selections as a real array.

name: Color Picker (item type)
apex: Lets the user pick or type a color via a popup/inline spectrum, a color-only popup button, or the browser's native color input.
attributes: Display As: Popup/Inline/Color-only Popup/Native Color Picker
Color Preset: None/Theme Style Colors/Custom Colors
Return Value As: Hex/rgb/rgb(a)/hsl/hsl(a)/Any CSS Value
workflow: Developer picks a Display As style, optionally offers preset swatches, and sets Return Value As to control the stored color format.

name: Combobox (item type)
apex: A text field with an LOV-backed suggestion dropdown that also accepts free text typed by the user; supports multi-select chips and search-as-you-type.
attributes: Search: Contains/Starts With, Case-Sensitive, minimum Characters
workflow: Developer defines a List of Values, picks Fetch on Search for large sets, and sets a Manual Entries Item to capture free-text values not in the LOV.

name: Date Picker (item type)
apex: A text field plus calendar icon for picking a date (and optionally time), shown as a popup, always inline, or via the browser's native date input.
workflow: Developer sets Display As for the interaction style, optional Min/Max Date bounds, and a Format Mask controlling the stored/displayed date pattern.
skip_for_web: Native HTML mode's format mask is browser-locked by APEX; a JS date-picker library exposes this directly instead of hiding it behind a mode switch.

name: Date Picker (jQuery) (item type, desupported)
apex: The legacy jQuery-based date picker, superseded by the current Date Picker item type; kept only for apps not yet upgraded, since upgrading may lose customizations.
attributes: Settings, Display As: Popup Calendar/Inline/Native HTML
workflow: Developer runs Utilities > Upgrade Application to migrate existing jQuery date pickers to the current item type rather than building new ones with it.
skip_for_web: Purely an Oracle backward-compatibility shim during a widget-library migration; irrelevant when building a component vocabulary from scratch.

name: Default (item value source)
apex: Sets an item's initial value when session state has no source value: from a static string, another item, a SQL query, a colon-delimited SQL list, a PL/SQL expression/function body, or a sequence.
attributes: Default, Type: SQL Query returning Colon Delimited List
workflow: Developer picks a Default Type matching how the initial value should be computed; it only applies when the item's real Source is null.
skip_for_web: SQL/PL-SQL-computed defaults run server-side against Oracle; a JS component instead takes an initialValue prop or fetches one client- or server-side.

name: Display Image (item type)
apex: Renders an image read from a database BLOB column or an image URL; not usable inside an interactive grid column.
workflow: Developer points Based On at the BLOB/URL source and names the companion columns (filename, MIME type, alt text, last-updated) that go with it for correct download and caching.
skip_for_web: BLOB-column image storage plus a last-updated column for browser caching is Oracle's DB-centric asset model; a JS app serves images from object storage/CDN URLs instead.

name: Display Map (item type)
apex: Shows a single-point map from a GeoJSON coordinate value on the item, with a chosen basemap, marker and optional zoom/rotation controls.
attributes: Settings, Background (Default/OpenStreetMap Bright/Dark/Positron/Oracle World Map/Shared Component)
workflow: Developer feeds the item a GeoJSON Point value, chooses a Background basemap, and toggles Interactive Map off for a static, non-pannable preview.

name: Display Only (item type)
apex: Shows a value as non-enterable text, optionally mapped through a List of Values, formatted as plain text, HTML or Markdown.
attributes: Settings, Based On: Page Item Value/Display Value of List of Values
workflow: Developer sets Based On to show either the raw value or its LOV display label, and enables Send On Page Submit only if the value must post back.

name: File Upload (item type)
apex: A Browse control for uploading one or more files from the local device, shown inline, as a dropzone, or via the browser's native picker; not usable in interactive grid columns.
attributes: Display, Display As: Inline File Browse/Inline Dropzone/Block Dropzone/Native File Browse
Storage, Type: BLOB column in Item Source / Table APEX_APPLICATION_TEMP_FILES
MIME Type / Filename / Character Set / BLOB Last Updated Column
workflow: Developer picks a Display As style, chooses whether uploads land in a BLOB column or the temp-files table, and sets file-type/size limits.
skip_for_web: Storing uploads in an APEX temp-files table or a row's BLOB column is Oracle's DB-resident file model; a JS app streams uploads to object storage (S3/R2/Blob) instead.

name: Format Mask (item Appearance attribute)
apex: An Appearance-group attribute that overrides APEX's automatic globalization-based formatting for numbers and dates on a specific item, forcing a fixed display format regardless of the user's browser language.
workflow: Developer selects the item in Page Designer and sets Appearance > Format Mask when the default locale-driven date/number formatting isn't what's wanted.

name: Geocoded Address (item type)
apex: Converts a postal address entered across other items into a GeoJSON coordinate via a browser-side call to Oracle's Elocation geocoding service, structured (separate Street/City/etc items) or unstructured (one comma-separated item).
attributes: Settings, Street/House Number/Postal Code/City/City Sub Area Item
Settings, Trigger Geocoding: Automatic/Dynamic Action/jQuery Selector
workflow: Developer maps up to eight address-part items (structured) or one free-text item (unstructured), then triggers geocoding to populate a coordinate item.
skip_for_web: Calls Oracle's own Elocation REST service from the browser; a JS app would call a geocoding provider (Google/Mapbox/etc.) of its choice directly.

name: Hidden (item type)
apex: An item present in the page source and session state but never rendered visually; carries values needed by processing without user interaction.
workflow: Developer uses a hidden item to pass an id or flag between page load and processing, enabling Value Protected to stop it being tampered with on post.

name: Image Upload (item type)
apex: Uploads one or more images with an optional crop step and client-side resize; previews after upload/crop. Cropping is not supported together with Allow Multiple Files.
attributes: Display, Display As: Inline File Browse/Icon Dropzone/Inline Dropzone/Block Dropzone/Native File Browse
workflow: Developer picks a Display As style, turns on Cropping with an Aspect Ratio for consistent thumbnails, and sets Resize To limits to shrink oversized uploads client-side.

name: Item Naming Conventions
apex: Rules for naming an item: unique per app, no quotes, starts with letter/number then letters/numbers/underscore, case-insensitive, max 30 chars, ASCII only. Convention: P<page>_<NAME>.
workflow: Developer names each item following the convention so it can be referenced by bind-variable syntax; wizards auto-prefix it with the page number.
skip_for_web: The 30-char/bind-variable-syntax ceiling is an Oracle SQL/PLSQL binding limit; JS identifiers have no such constraint.

name: Item Security group
apex: Controls who can render/execute the item and how its session-state value may be set: an authorization scheme gate, URL/POST tamper protection tiers, encryption at rest, and a character allow/blocklist.
attributes: Security, Session State Protection: Unrestricted / Checksum Required (Application, User, Session Level) / Restricted
Security, Store value encrypted in session state
workflow: Developer assigns an Authorization Scheme to gate visibility, sets Session State Protection to stop URL/POST tampering, and enables encryption or a character restriction for sensitive input.
skip_for_web: Checksum-guarded URL state-setting defends Oracle's f?p link format; a JS app validates/authorizes on its API layer instead, and encrypts at the database/column level, not per form field.

name: Item Server-side Condition
apex: A condition type that must evaluate true at render time for the item to be shown/processed at all; an unmet condition removes the item entirely, not just disables it.
workflow: Developer picks a condition type (e.g. item value comparison, PL/SQL expression) so the item only renders when the business rule holds.

name: List Manager (item type)
apex: An LOV-backed text item with Add/Remove buttons that builds a list of selected values, typed or picked from a popup; stored as one colon-delimited string. Not supported in interactive grid columns.
workflow: Developer attaches a LOV and lets the user add/remove entries one at a time into a running selected-values list.

name: Markdown Editor (item type)
apex: A text editor for writing Markdown-formatted content with an optional formatting toolbar and syntax highlighting; not supported in interactive grid columns.
workflow: Developer picks a Toolbar level matching how much formatting help authors need, and stores the raw Markdown as the item's value.

name: Multiple Values (item group)
apex: Tells a multi-select-capable item (Checkbox Group, List Manager, Popup LOV, Select List, Select Many, Shuttle, Combobox) how its stored column encodes several values: not multiple, a delimited string, or a JSON array, plus which delimiter.
workflow: Developer sets Type to match how the source column stores multi-select data, and Separator to the delimiter character, so APEX can parse and re-serialize selections.
skip_for_web: Delimited-string/JSON-in-a-column encoding works around SQL columns being scalar; a JS app's data layer typically stores a real array/relation instead.

name: Number Field (item type)
apex: A numeric text input with automatic client+server number validation and formatting; precision is capped around 15-17 digits by JS's IEEE 754 floats, so very large-number keys should use Text Field instead.
workflow: Developer sets a Format Mask for display, Min/Max Value bounds, and a Virtual Keyboard type for touch devices.
skip_for_web: The 15-17 digit IEEE-754 ceiling is a JavaScript number-representation limit baked into the widget; a JS app hits the same ceiling and already knows to route huge keys to a text/string field.

name: Page Item
apex: A single form control on a page: checkbox, date picker, file browse, popup LOV, select list, shuttle, switch, text field, textarea, etc. Holds a value in session state and carries UI properties (label, display-only, template).
workflow: Developer adds an item via the Rendering tab or the Gallery inside a region, names it (convention P<page>_<name>), sets its Type, and configures Source to control its value.

name: Page Item vs Application Item
apex: Page items live on a page and carry UI properties (Display Only, Label, Label Template); application items have no page or UI and act as global session-state variables usable anywhere in the app.
workflow: Developer uses a page item for anything the user sees or edits, and an application item purely to carry a value between pages/processes with no rendering.
skip_for_web: Both are Oracle server-session-state slots; a JS app holds page-local state in component state and cross-page/global state in a store or URL/cookie, with no separate 'has no UI' variable kind needed.

name: Password (item type)
apex: A masked text input for sensitive values; each typed character shows as a dot. Best combined with memory-only session storage and encryption if persisted.
attributes: Appearance, Template Options, Hide Password Visibility
Session State, Storage: Per Request (Memory Only) recommended
Security, Store value encrypted in session state
workflow: Developer sets Storage to Per Request for highly sensitive values, or enables encrypted session-state storage when the value must persist.

name: Percent Graph (item type)
apex: Renders a numeric value (0-100) as a horizontal percentage bar instead of raw text.
workflow: Developer points the item's Source at a numeric percentage column; no further attributes are documented beyond the value range.

name: Popup LOV (item type)
apex: A text field with an icon that opens a searchable popup list, best for large value sets (versus Select List for small ones); can allow typed manual entry alongside picking.
attributes: Search: Contains/Starts With, Case-Sensitive, minimum Characters
Multiple Values, Type: No/Delimited List/JSON Array
workflow: Developer defines a LOV with aliased display/return columns, sets a minimum-Characters threshold for expensive queries, and decides whether Manual Entry is allowed.

name: QR Code (item type)
apex: Encodes the item's source value as a scannable QR code image, with a Data Type prefix that tells the scanner app how to act on it (plain text, phone, email, SMS, geo location).
attributes: QR Code, Data Type: Plain Text/Phone/Email/SMS/Geo location
workflow: Developer sets Data Type to match the value's meaning (e.g. Email) so scanning phones open the right app, and picks a Size.

name: Quick Picks
apex: One-click preset value buttons shown beside an item so users pick a common value instead of typing or opening a list, sourced from up to 10 static pairs, a shared LOV's ranked entries, or a SQL query.
attributes: Quick Picks, Label N / Value N (up to 10)
Quick Picks, Type: Shared List of Values
workflow: Developer sets Quick Picks, Type on a supported item and supplies static label/value pairs, or points at a shared LOV's Quick Pick Rank column, or a SQL query.

name: Radio Group (item type)
apex: Renders a List of Values as mutually-exclusive radio buttons for single-value selection, optionally laid out in multiple columns.
attributes: Settings, Execute Validations (when action is Submit Page)
workflow: Developer attaches a LOV, sets Number of Columns for layout, and optionally makes selecting a value submit the page.

name: Read Only (item attribute)
apex: A condition type that, when true, renders an enterable item as non-editable (styled like Display Only) while still showing it; Type=Never forces it always editable, overriding page/region-level read-only.
workflow: Developer sets a Read Only condition (e.g. based on another item's value or a role) instead of hard-coding Display Only, so editability can vary per record or user.

name: Referencing Item Values
apex: Four ways to read/write an item's session-state value depending on context: SQL bind variable, PL/SQL V()/NV() functions, static-text substitution, or JavaScript $v()/$s().
workflow: Developer picks the syntax matching where the reference is written (SQL query, PL/SQL block, template text, or JS code) to read or set an item's current value.
skip_for_web: V()/NV()/bind-variable/substitution syntaxes are all reads of Oracle's server-side session-state table; a JS app just reads component state or a client store directly, and $v/$s become plain getState/setState.

name: Rich Text Editor (item type)
apex: A WYSIWYG text area with word-processor-style formatting, storing content as HTML or Markdown; supports pasting RTF content.
workflow: Developer picks Format (HTML for richer output, Markdown for safer storage) and a Toolbar level matching the formatting options end users need.

name: Select List (item type)
apex: A native inline dropdown built from a List of Values; best for small, discrete option sets (use Popup LOV or Select Many/One for larger sets).
attributes: Settings, Execute Validations (when action is Submit Page)
workflow: Developer attaches a small LOV and optionally sets Page Action on Selection to Submit Page so choosing a value immediately reloads/processes the page.

name: Select Many (item type)
apex: A modern multi-select dropdown with search filtering, grouping and chip/comma display, more user-friendly than a Popup LOV for multiple values.
attributes: Settings, Display Values As: Chips/Comma-separated list
Search: Contains/Starts With, Case-Sensitive, minimum Characters
Multiple Values, Type: Delimited List/JSON Array
workflow: Developer defines a LOV, turns on Fetch on Search for large sets, and sets Display Values As to control how selections render when unfocused.

name: Select One (item type)
apex: A modern single-value dropdown with search filtering, groups and template directives; a more user-friendly alternative to Select List.
attributes: Search: Contains/Starts With, Case-Sensitive, minimum Characters
workflow: Developer defines a LOV and enables Fetch on Search for large option sets so the dropdown queries the database as the user types.

name: Session State Storage (item)
apex: Governs where an item's value is kept between requests: memory-only for the current request, persisted per session, or persisted per user across sessions.
attributes: Session State, Storage: Per Request (Memory Only)
workflow: Developer chooses Per Request for pure Ajax/transient values (passing them via Page Items to Submit), or a Disk option when the value must survive page navigation.
skip_for_web: This is Oracle's own server-held session table; a JS app keeps transient values in component/store state and persistent ones in its own database or cookie/JWT.

name: Shuttle (item type)
apex: Two side-by-side list boxes (available vs selected) with move controls between them; selected values are stored as one colon-delimited string.
attributes: Settings, Show Controls: None/Moving Only/Ordering Only/All
workflow: Developer attaches a LOV and picks which shuttle controls (move, reorder) are shown between the two list boxes.

name: Star Rating (item type)
apex: A clickable row of up to 10 icons (default 5) that sets a numeric value; icon, colors and tooltip are customizable, and read-only display can show stars, the value, or both.
attributes: Read Only Display: Stars/Value/Stars and Value/Single Star and Value
workflow: Developer sets Number of Stars and, if not using shared defaults, picks an Icon and colors matching the app's theme.

name: Switch (item type)
apex: A binary flip-toggle (can also render as a Pill Button or Select List) mapping On/Off states to two stored values with their own labels.
workflow: Developer sets On/Off Value and Label pairs, or leaves Use Defaults on to inherit the app's shared Switch component settings.

name: Text Field (item type)
apex: The baseline single-line text input; Subtype picks an HTML5 input flavor (email, url, tel, etc.) for better mobile keyboards, and can transform case or trim whitespace.
attributes: Settings, Trim Spaces: Leading/Trailing/Leading and Trailing/None
workflow: Developer sets Subtype to match the expected data (email, phone, etc.) so mobile devices show the right keyboard and read-only rendering links correctly.

name: Text Field with Autocomplete (item type)
apex: A text field showing an inline suggestion list drawn from a SQL query, refined as the user types further characters.
attributes: Search mode: Contains/Exact x Case Sensitive/Ignore Case
workflow: Developer writes a single-column SQL query as the source and enables Fetch On Type for large candidate sets so matches are queried live.

name: Textarea (item type)
apex: A multi-row plain text input box, optionally resizable, auto-growing to content, with a character counter and whitespace trimming.
attributes: Settings, Trim Spaces: Leading/Trailing/Leading and Trailing/None
workflow: Developer enables Auto-Height for growing content or sets a fixed Resizable box, and turns on Character Counter for length-sensitive fields.

name: Warn on Unsaved Changes (item)
apex: Advanced-group flag deciding whether edits to this item count toward the page's leave-without-saving browser warning; items not tied to a database column are usually set to Ignore.
attributes: Advanced, Warn on Unsaved Changes: Page Default
Advanced, Warn on Unsaved Changes: Ignore
workflow: Developer leaves Page Default for real data-entry items and sets Ignore on non-persisted items like a search box so they don't trigger false unsaved-changes warnings.

name: Copying a Region
apex: Duplicates an existing region, either to another position on the same page (Layout tab, right-click, Copy To) or to a different page entirely (Rendering tab, right-click, Copy to Other Page). Tree regions cannot be copied.
workflow: Developer right-clicks a region and chooses a copy destination instead of rebuilding it from scratch.

name: Creating a Region (Page Designer)
apex: Regions are added manually in Page Designer either from the Rendering tab (right-click a container, Create Region) or from the Gallery (right-click a region type tile).
workflow: Developer right-clicks in Rendering tab or picks from Gallery, sets Title and Type, then edits the Type-specific attributes that appear, and saves.
skip_for_web: Legacy region types (deprecated but still supported) are an Oracle upgrade-compatibility concern, not relevant when designing a new component vocabulary.

name: Deleting Regions
apex: Removes one or more regions from a page via the Rendering tab: select, right-click, Delete, Save.
workflow: Developer selects region(s) in the Rendering tab, right-clicks Delete, and saves the page.

name: Global Page
apex: A special page (historically Page 0) whose regions, items and buttons render on every page of the application, used for components like a persistent header, footer or navigation bar.
workflow: Developer designates one page as the application's global page in the app definition; anything placed on it appears app-wide.

name: Item Layout (Region + Position)
apex: An item's Layout group assigns which region contains it (blank means page level) and a Position slot placing it precisely within that region or page.
workflow: Developer sets Layout, Region to attach an item to a region (or leaves it empty for page-level placement), then sets Layout, Position to place it exactly.

name: Page Layout Model
apex: Pages render by combining a page template (overall structure: tabs, nav bar, region positions) with regions (content containers, styled by region templates) and data.
workflow: Developer picks a page template for overall structure, then places each region either in a named region position or by sequence/column ordering.

name: Parent Region (nesting)
apex: A Layout-group attribute that nests one region completely inside another named parent region, rather than placing it independently on the page grid.
attributes: Layout, Position (template position within the parent)
workflow: Developer sets Layout, Parent Region on a child region (e.g. a Tree, or any nested region) so it renders inside the chosen container instead of at the page's top grid level.

name: Parent/Child Data in Regions (BOSS REST nesting)
apex: Despite the filename, this page covers nesting Oracle Cloud Applications BOSS REST resources (e.g. Order to OrderLine to OrderLineFulfillment) via parameterized URL paths, not master-detail page regions.
attributes: REST Data Source URL path parameter, e.g. /orders/:orderId/orderLines
Parameters node (Rendering tab) binds a path parameter to a page item
workflow: Developer defines a REST Data Source with named URL path parameters for nested resources, then binds each parameter to a page item under the region's Parameters node so the region fetches the right child records.
skip_for_web: Oracle Cloud Applications BOSS REST integration is a niche enterprise-ERP data source; a JS app builds general master-detail with normal nested API routes/foreign keys instead.

name: Region
apex: A container area on a page holding content: HTML, a report, a form, chart, list, breadcrumb, PL/SQL, tree, URL, or calendar. Every page has one or more regions; a region template controls border, background, fonts and button placement.
attributes: Sequence/Column position or named region position
workflow: Developer adds a region to a page, sets its Type and Template, then places page items/buttons/reports inside it.

name: Region Grid Layout (Start New Row, Column, Span, Sequence)
apex: The Universal Theme lays regions on a 12-column responsive grid; per-region Layout attributes place it there (start column, column/row span, force new row, extra CSS classes), plus Sequence and Parent Region. Per-attribute mechanics not detailed in docs read.
attributes: Layout, Position (named template/region position, alternative to grid placement)
workflow: Developer either lets a region flow in Sequence order on the grid (setting Column/Span/Start New Row), or bypasses the grid by placing it into a named template Position instead.
skip_for_web: A DIV-based 12-column grid substituting for the pre-Universal-Theme HTML-table layout is Oracle's own CSS grid convention; a JS app just uses CSS Grid/Flexbox directly with no APEX-specific attribute names.

name: Tabs
apex: Legacy top-of-page navigation control (pre-Universal-Theme). Two levels: Parent tabs (select a standard tab set) and Standard tabs (map 1:1 to a page). Superseded by list-based navigation menus in Universal Theme 42.
workflow: Developer opens Shared Components > Tabs, adds a Parent tab and/or Standard tabs, associates each Standard tab with a page; the active theme's page template must define tab positions for them to render.
skip_for_web: Theme-era HTML-table navigation tied to Oracle's older page templates; a modern site uses a nav component driven by a list of routes instead.

name: Cascading List of Values
apex: A dependent item whose LOV re-queries when a separate parent item's value changes, e.g. an Employee select list filtered by the chosen Department. Supported on Select List, Shuttle, Checkbox, Radio Group, Popup LOV, List Manager.
attributes: List of Values, SQL Query referencing the parent item, e.g. :P1_DEPTNO
List of Values, Display Null Value
List of Values, Null Display Value
workflow: Developer builds the child item's LOV as a SQL query that binds the parent item, and/or sets Cascading LOV Parent Item so APEX Ajax-refreshes the child list whenever the parent changes.

name: List of Values (LOV)
apex: A static or dynamic value/display-label list bound to page items that offer choices: select list, radio group, checkbox, popup LOV, multiple select. Can be defined locally on one item or shared across the app.
attributes: Type: local data source / REST Enabled SQL / REST Data Source (dynamic, shared only)
Shared LOV extras: multi-column, icon column, grouping column
workflow: Developer either builds the LOV inline on the item (List of Values group) for one-off use, or creates a named LOV under Shared Components once and points multiple items at it.

name: Static List of Values
apex: A hand-entered list of Display Value/Return Value pairs stored inline on one item (not reusable); order is manual unless Sort at Runtime is enabled to alphabetize at render time.
attributes: List of Values, Type: Static Values
workflow: Developer sets Identification, Type to a choice item, List of Values Type to Static Values, opens the Static Values dialog and enters Display/Return pairs.

name: Map (region type)
apex: Plots spatial geometry (points, lines, polygons, heat maps, extruded 3D polygons) over a static background map from Oracle's Elocation service (raster or vector tile layers), sourced from a local table, REST Enabled SQL, or REST Data Source.
attributes: Layers (one or more spatial geometry layers)
Attributes tab: Initial Position and Zoom
workflow: Developer adds a Map region, sets its background/controls at the region-Attributes level, then adds one or more Layers for the actual geometry data.
skip_for_web: Background tiles come from Oracle's own Elocation/maps.oracle.com service requiring outbound browser access to that domain; a JS app picks its own map/tile provider (Mapbox, Leaflet+OSM, Google Maps).

name: Map Controls
apex: Runtime UI chrome for a map, individually toggled: navigation bar (zoom/compass), rectangle zoom, current-location, circle-draw and distance tools, tooltip, overview inset, scale bar, and legend.
attributes: Controls, Navigation Bar: None/Zoom Only/Zoom and Compass
workflow: Developer enables only the controls end users need; Infinite Map and Bounding Box are mutually exclusive (disable Infinite Map to define a Bounding Box).

name: Map Initial Position, Zoom and Bounding Box
apex: Controls where a map opens and how far a user can pan/zoom: an initial position/zoom rule (remembered per session thereafter), and an optional bounding box restricting the visible extent.
attributes: Initial Position and Zoom, Zoom Level (1-24)
Bounding Box, Type: None/Static Values/SQL Query
workflow: Developer sets Initial Position and Zoom for first load, and optionally a Bounding Box (only when Infinite Map is off) to keep users within a fixed area.

name: Map Layer
apex: One spatial geometry data set drawn on a map: its own Source (table/query/REST), a Column Mapping (geometry column or two lat/long numeric columns) and a Layer Type (Points, Lines, Polygons, Heat Map, or Extruded Polygons).
attributes: Identification, Layer Type: Points/Lines/Polygons/Heat Map/Extruded Polygons
Column Mapping, Geometry Column Data Type: SDO_GEOMETRY/GeoJSON/Longitude-Latitude
workflow: Developer right-clicks Layers, Create Layer, sets its Source and Column Mapping, and picks a Layer Type matching the geometry shape being plotted.
skip_for_web: SDO_GEOMETRY is Oracle Spatial's native column type; a JS app stores geometry as GeoJSON (already a supported alternative here) in an ordinary column instead.

name: Map Layer Styling (Appearance/Tooltip/Info Window/Legend)
apex: Per-layer presentation: fill/stroke color and opacity, a hover Tooltip, a click Info Window, a visible Zoom Levels range, and a Legend entry, each optionally driven by an HTML expression with column substitutions instead of a fixed template.
attributes: Appearance, Fill Color/Fill Opacity/Stroke Color/Stroke Width (support substitutions)
Tooltip, Advanced Formatting / HTML Expression / CSS Classes
Info Window, Title Column / Body Column
Legend, Show / Advanced Formatting / Enable to Hide / Icon CSS Classes
workflow: Developer styles a layer's fill/stroke, writes a Tooltip/Info Window (plain column or HTML expression), sets its visible Zoom Levels range, and configures its Legend entry.

name: Map-to-Report Sync Pattern
apex: A worked pattern linking a map's visible extent to a report: a hidden item stores the map's current bounds (Advanced, Bounding Box Item), the report's SQL filters by that bound, and a Map Changed dynamic action refreshes/shows/hides the report as the user pans or zooms.
attributes: Map Attributes, Advanced, Bounding Box Item
Dynamic Action, When Event: Map Changed [Map]
Report Source, Page Items to Submit
Report SQL using sdo_anyinteract(...) against the bound item
workflow: Developer wires a hidden PX_BBOX item as the map's Bounding Box Item, filters the report query by it, and adds a Map Changed dynamic action to refresh the report on pan/zoom.
skip_for_web: sdo_anyinteract spatial filtering is Oracle Spatial SQL; a JS map (Mapbox/Leaflet) fires a moveend event with the same bounds for a client fetch against any backend's bbox query instead.

name: Region Accessibility group
apex: A Property Editor group of attributes aimed at assistive-technology users (e.g. screen readers), letting a region carry accessibility metadata beyond its visual template.
attributes: Accessibility group (specific attributes not itemized in the docs read)
workflow: Developer reviews the Accessibility group for any region intended to be navigated by assistive technology.

name: Region Advanced group
apex: Low-level hooks: an HTML DOM ID for custom CSS/JS targeting (via #DOM_ID#, replacing the deprecated #REGION_STATIC_ID#), free-form Custom Attributes injected via #REGION_ATTRIBUTES#, a Static ID for API/export references, a Region Display Selector on/off flag, and Exclude Title from Translation.
workflow: Developer sets HTML DOM ID when custom CSS/JS needs a stable hook, and turns on Region Display Selector only when a Region Display Selector region exists on the same page.

name: Region Appearance group
apex: Controls a region's visual template, which determines border, background, title placement and button-position layout; Template Options then fine-tune look within that template.
workflow: Developer picks a region Template matching the desired container style (e.g. a bordered box, no title, collapsible).

name: Region Attributes tab (type-specific settings)
apex: The Property Editor's second tab (labelled Attributes) holding settings unique to the region's Type, distinct from the generic Region tab groups shared by every region type.
attributes: Calendar Attributes: Display Column, Start Date Column, ...
Map Attributes: Controls, Initial Position and Zoom, Bounding Box, ...
Tree Attributes: Node Label Column, Hierarchy, ...
workflow: Developer switches to the Attributes tab whenever they need region-type-specific behavior, after finishing the generic Region tab (Identification/Source/Layout/etc).

name: Region Configuration group
