apex: Ties a component to a Build Option, a predefined named flag that enables or disables groups of components together, letting a developer stage or environment-gate features declaratively.
workflow: Developer assigns a Build Option to regions that belong to an in-progress or environment-specific feature, then flips that one Build Option to enable/disable them all.

name: Region Customization group (end-user layout)
apex: Lets end users show/hide a region themselves at runtime via a Customize link, which only appears if the page template includes the #CUSTOMIZE# substitution string.
attributes: Customization, Customizable: Not Customizable By End Users
Customization, Customizable: Customizable and Not Shown By Default
Customization, Customizable: Customizable and Shown By Default
workflow: Developer marks optional/secondary regions Customizable so users can personalize which ones they see, provided the page template supports #CUSTOMIZE#.

name: Region Header and Footer group
apex: Extra HTML placed just above (Header Text) or below (Footer Text) the region's body content; classic-report footers additionally support row-count substitution strings.
workflow: Developer writes Header/Footer Text with these substitution tokens to show render-time diagnostics or a rows-X-Y-of-Z summary under a classic report.

name: Region Identification group
apex: Names and titles a region: Name is the required internal identifier shown in the Rendering/Layout tabs; Title is the optional display heading (falls back to Name at runtime if the region template doesn't show a title, or the title is empty).
workflow: Developer sets Name when creating the region, and a Title only if the chosen region template renders one.

name: Region Image (Advanced)
apex: Adds a single image to the upper-left of a region's template, with optional HTML tag attributes (size, alt text); no ALT means the image renders as decorative.
workflow: Developer enters an image reference and, for meaningful (non-decorative) images, sets an ALT attribute via Image Tag Attributes.

name: Region Layout group (Position)
apex: Places a region either by flowing it in Sequence/grid order, or by assigning Layout, Position to a named slot the current page or region template defines.
attributes: Layout, Region (for items, which region they belong to)
workflow: Developer leaves Position unset to let the region flow in the grid by Sequence, or picks a named template Position for exact placement (e.g. a sidebar slot).

name: Region Security group
apex: Gates a region behind an Authorization Scheme that must evaluate to TRUE for it to render or process at all; the same group name and attribute is used for items, buttons and regions alike.
workflow: Developer assigns a shared Authorization Scheme (defined once under Shared Components) to any region that should be restricted to certain roles/users.

name: Region Server Cache group (region caching)
apex: Caches a rendered region instead of recomputing it every request, useful for static content like unconditioned lists; the actual session id is never cached, only a substitution token swapped in per viewer.
attributes: Server Cache, Caching: Enabled (shared by all users)
Server Cache, Caching: Cached by User
Server Cache, Caching: Cache by Session
workflow: Developer enables caching on regions whose content rarely changes, scoping it per-user or per-session when the content still varies by viewer.

name: Region Server-side Condition group
apex: A condition (e.g. Expression, PL/SQL) that must evaluate true for the region (or a map layer, which uses the identical group) to render at all; APEX applies this on layers with an Execute Condition of For Each Row.
attributes: Server-side Condition, Execute Condition: For Each Row
workflow: Developer sets a condition type and expression so the whole region (or layer) disappears server-side when the rule is false, rather than just being styled hidden.

name: Region Source group
apex: Where and how a region's data is fetched: Location picks the origin (local database, REST Enabled SQL, REST Data Source, Duality View, JSON Source, or sample data); Type picks the query mechanism (table/view, SQL query, or function body).
attributes: Source, Location: Local Database/REST Enabled SQL/REST Source/Duality View/JSON Source/Sample Data
Source, Type: Table/View/SQL Query/Function Body returning SQL Query
workflow: Developer sets Location first, which determines what Type options and follow-on fields (table name, query text) appear next.

name: Breadcrumb (region type)
apex: Displays the current page's breadcrumb trail (the path of parent pages leading to it) as a region.
workflow: Developer adds a Breadcrumb region to a page template or page so the page's position in the navigation hierarchy is visible.

name: Cards (region type)
apex: A SQL-query-driven report shown as a tiled grid of information cards, in a Grid, Float, or Horizontal (Row) layout, with declaratively customizable Header, Media, Body and Actions per card.
workflow: Developer builds a Cards region over a SQL query and maps columns into the Header/Media/Body/Actions template slots instead of a classic table layout.

name: Classic Report (region type)
apex: A simple SQL-query report without the interactive customization features (sort/filter/save) of an Interactive Report; a lighter-weight tabular display.
attributes: (fewer end-user customization options than Interactive Report)
workflow: Developer picks Classic Report when a plain, non-customizable table is enough and Interactive Report's toolbar/features aren't wanted.

name: Dynamic Content / PL/SQL Dynamic Content (region type)
apex: Displays HTML markup returned at render time by a PL/SQL function, for output not achievable with a standard report/form region.
attributes: Source: PL/SQL Function Body returning HTML
workflow: Developer writes a PL/SQL function body that returns HTML and sets it as the region's source when no built-in region type fits.
skip_for_web: Generating markup from a server-side PL/SQL function is Oracle's escape hatch for custom output; a JS app just writes the component/template directly, no equivalent indirection needed.

name: Faceted Search (region type)
apex: An ecommerce-style filter-and-browse UI: a panel of facet filters alongside a results area rendered as cards or a classic report.
attributes: Results display: Cards or Classic Report
workflow: Developer adds a Faceted Search region over a data source and defines facets (filterable columns) plus the results display style.

name: Form (region type)
apex: A container for data-entry page items bound to one row of a data source (local, remote, or REST); each item is assigned to both a Form region (for data binding) and a display region (for layout).
attributes: Items assigned to this Form region
workflow: Developer creates a Form region bound to a table/service, then assigns each page item to it as its data-binding region while placing the item visually in another region.

name: Help Text (region type)
apex: A special region type used only on an application's dedicated Help page, to render field-level help content.
attributes: (used on the dedicated Help page only)
workflow: Developer relies on this region type when building/customizing the app's built-in Help page rather than placing it on ordinary pages.

name: Interactive Grid (region type)
apex: A searchable, end-user-customizable spreadsheet-like report supporting inline edit and mouse/keyboard rearrangement, so one grid definition serves many ad hoc viewing/editing needs instead of several fixed reports.
attributes: (same customization options as Interactive Report, plus interactive rearrange/edit)
workflow: Developer defines one Interactive Grid over a data source and lets end users sort, filter, group, and rearrange columns/rows themselves at runtime.

name: Interactive Report (region type)
apex: A SQL-query report with a rich end-user toolbar (search, filter, sort, save reports, charts, etc); developers can enable/disable which customization features are exposed.
workflow: Developer builds one Interactive Report and controls the toolbar features available so end users self-serve their own view instead of needing separate report variants.

name: List (region type)
apex: Renders a static or dynamic List (a shared list of label+target entries) as a region, typically for navigating between pages.
attributes: List source: Static or Dynamic (shared List component)
workflow: Developer creates or reuses a shared List (Shared Components) and displays it via a List region, commonly for a nav menu or link panel.

name: Reflow Report (region type, legacy)
apex: A responsive report that reflows from a column layout to a stacked row layout on smaller screens; documented as a legacy option.
workflow: Developer picks this only for legacy responsive-report needs; newer responsive patterns (Cards, Interactive Grid) are the current recommendation.

name: Region Display Selector (region type)
apex: A navigation region listing other regions by name as tabs; clicking one shows just that region and hides the rest (plus a first Show All entry). Only regions with their own Region Display Selector attribute set On appear in the list.
attributes: Attributes, Settings, Mode: View Single Region/Scroll Window
Attributes, Settings, Remember Last Selection: By User/By Session/No
workflow: Developer adds a Region Display Selector region, then turns On its Advanced, Region Display Selector attribute on every region that should be selectable from it.

name: Region Type Plug-ins
apex: Third-party or custom region types installed into an app, appearing in the Gallery named '<Name> [Plug-in]'. Built-in examples: Avatar, Badge, Comments, Content Row, Media List, Sample Apps Footer, Source Display, Timeline.
attributes: Badge: content in a badge, single or multi-row
Comments: comments/status updates with avatars, single row or report
Content Row: formatted row with title/description/avatars/badges
Media List: formatted media list with avatars/badges
Timeline: series of events with avatars/badges
Source Display: shows an accompanying region's SQL source
workflow: Developer drags a plug-in region from the Gallery like any built-in type; plug-ins ship with the app's shared components and can be customized or replaced.
skip_for_web: APEX's plug-in packaging (PL/SQL render/AJAX callbacks registered as a component type) is Oracle-specific; a JS component library just adds a new component to its own registry.

name: Smart Filters (region type)
apex: A single top-of-page search field paired with a results report (classic report, cards, map, or calendar); like Faceted Search but in a more compact, space-efficient layout.
workflow: Developer picks Smart Filters over Faceted Search when screen space is tighter but a similar filter-and-browse experience is wanted.

name: Static Content (region type)
apex: Displays fixed text/HTML content, or serves as a plain container for page items; set Output As to HTML to render markup unescaped.
workflow: Developer uses Static Content for hand-written text/HTML blocks or as a bare container to group items with no report/form behavior.

name: URL (region type, detail)
apex: Displays remote content fetched from a URL, e.g. embedding a page item's value into the address. Content can be shown as an iframe or fetched server-side and inlined.
attributes: URL (discard until but not including this text)
URL (discard after and including this text)
Proxy Server (application attribute, needed for outbound fetch)
workflow: Developer creates a Type=URL region, enters the target URL (optionally embedding &ITEM_NAME. substitutions), trims unwanted HTML with the discard-text attributes, and picks an Inclusion Mode.
skip_for_web: Server-side HTML fetch-and-inline via utl_http and a DB-stored SSL wallet is an Oracle-specific proxy pattern; a JS app just fetches or iframes the URL directly from the client or an edge function.

name: Workflow Diagram (region type)
apex: A read-only visual diagram of a running workflow's progress and completed activities.
workflow: Developer adds this region on a page tracking a specific workflow instance to visualize its state.
skip_for_web: APEX's built-in Workflow engine (approvals, activities) is an Oracle-specific process-orchestration feature; a JS app would visualize its own workflow/state-machine library's state instead.

name: List Search
apex: A Search Configuration of Type List searches the entries of a shared APEX List (label + target page) rather than a table, useful for site-wide search-these-named-pages functionality.
attributes: Column Mapping: Primary Key/Title/Description Column (mapped from the List's own columns)
workflow: Developer first builds a static List of pages/labels under Shared Components, then creates a List-type Search Configuration pointing at it, then a Search page using it as a Search Source.

name: Search (region type / feature)
apex: A two-part declarative search: a reusable Search Configuration (Shared Components) describing one searchable data source, and a page's Search region binding a search-input item to one or more of those configurations as Search Sources.
attributes: Search Results region: Settings, Search Page Item
Search Results region: Pagination, Results per Page
workflow: Developer builds one Search Configuration per searchable table/list, then a Search page (wizard or manual) whose region lists those configurations as Search Sources.

name: Search Configuration (Shared Component)
apex: A named, reusable definition of one searchable data source, created once under Shared Components and referenced by any Search region's Search Source.
attributes: Search Type: Oracle TEXT (linguistic/fuzzy, needs a TEXT index)
Search Type: Oracle Ubiquitous Search (needs Oracle AI Database 26ai+)
Search Type: List (searches an APEX shared List)
Data Source: Local Database/REST Enabled SQL/REST Source/Duality View/JSON Source/Sample Data
workflow: Developer runs Shared Components > Search Configurations > Create, picks a Search Type matching the data and index available, then points it at a table, query, or List.
skip_for_web: Oracle TEXT and Oracle Ubiquitous Search depend on Oracle-specific database search indexes; a JS app would call an external search service (Algolia, Elasticsearch, Postgres full-text) instead.

name: Search Configuration Column Mapping
apex: Maps a searchable source's columns to the parts of a search-result card: which column is the unique key, which is the title, which is the description, and how its icon is rendered.
workflow: Developer maps Primary Key/Title/Description columns so each result renders as a titled card, and picks how its icon is derived (initials from the title, a fixed class, or a per-row class column).

name: Search Configuration Link
apex: Turns each search result into a link to another page, passing values (e.g. the row's key) as target-page items, with options to reset pagination or clear cached session state on the target page.
attributes: Link, Type: Redirect to Page in this Application (etc.)
Link, Set these items / With these values
Link, reset pagination for this page
workflow: Developer sets Link, Page and maps Set these items/With these values (e.g. &ID.) so clicking a result opens the right record on the target page.

name: Tree (region type)
apex: Displays hierarchical parent-child data as an expandable tree using the APEX Tree JS component (desktop UI only); the source query must use START WITH .. CONNECT BY, or APEX can compute the hierarchy itself from an ID/Parent Key pair.
workflow: Developer adds a Tree region, points its Source at a table/query with parent-child columns, then configures the tree-specific Attributes tab to map ID, parent and label columns.
skip_for_web: START WITH .. CONNECT BY is Oracle SQL's native recursive-hierarchy syntax; a JS app builds the tree from a recursive CTE or assembles nodes client-side from a flat parent-id list instead.

name: Tree Attributes (node mapping)
apex: Maps source columns to tree node parts and decides whether APEX computes the hierarchy itself (from an ID + Parent Key column) or the query already carries precomputed status/level columns.
attributes: Settings, Hierarchy: Computed With SQL / Not Computed
Computed: Node ID Column / Parent Key Column
Not Computed: Node Status Column (0=leaf,1=has children) / Hierarchy Level Column
workflow: Developer picks Hierarchy = Computed With SQL for a plain id/parent-id table (APEX derives structure), or Not Computed when the query already returns each row's status and depth.

name: Tree via Create Page Wizard (Start Tree)
apex: The wizard path to a Tree page: pick ID/Parent ID/Node Text/Start With columns, then choose how the root of the hierarchy is determined.
attributes: Start Tree: Based on Existing Item
Start Tree: Based on a SQL Query
Start Tree: Based on a Static Value
workflow: Developer runs Create Page > Tree, maps ID/Parent ID/Node Text, and sets Start Tree to fix which row the hierarchy begins from.

name: Branch (overview)
apex: An instruction to go to a specific page, procedure, or URL after a page event, e.g. from page 1 to page 2 after submit; defined by a Branch Point and Branch Type.
workflow: Developer adds a branch under Processing and sets where in the page lifecycle it fires (Branch Point) and its target (Branch Type).

name: Branch attributes: Point, Type, When Button Pressed
apex: A branch Point sets when in the page lifecycle it is considered; its Type sets the destination (page, URL, procedure); When Button Pressed restricts it to firing only after a specific button submits the page.
workflow: Developer right-clicks Rendering or Processing tree, Create Branch, sets Point and Type (Target if redirecting), and optionally scopes it via When Button Pressed or a Condition Type.
skip_for_web: Point names mirror Oracle APEX's page-submit lifecycle; a JS route handler just runs steps in code order, no named lifecycle points needed.

name: Card Actions
apex: A per-card interactive element (link or button) letting the user click through to detail; developer chooses which part of the card is clickable and where it goes.
attributes: Link Type: Redirect to Page in this Application
Link Type: Redirect to Page in different Application
Server-side Condition (Once vs For Each Row)
workflow: Developer right-clicks the cards region Actions node, adds an action, picks which card part triggers it and where it links; only Button actions repeat per row, others render once.
skip_for_web: Session-state Set Items/Clear Cache targeting page numbers is APEX page model; a JS card just needs an href or onClick to a route with query params.

name: Card Attribute Groups (Title/Subtitle/Body/Secondary Body/Icon/Badge/Media)
apex: Per-card content attributes edited in the Attributes tab: Appearance, Title, Subtitle, Body, Secondary Body, Icon and Badge, and Media, each normally mapped from a report column.
attributes: Advanced Formatting (HTML + substitution strings) on Title/Subtitle/Body/Secondary Body/Media
workflow: Developer maps each group to a column or static/HTML expression; free-text fields (CSS Classes, Icon/Image Description, Badge Label) accept column substitution strings.

name: Cards Region (overview)
apex: A report region rendering rows as an orderly layout of information tiles instead of a table, supporting icons, badges, media and click actions.
workflow: Developer picks a layout and maps columns to Title/Body/Media etc in region attributes; used for card-style browsing pages.

name: Classic Report (overview)
apex: A simple report page rendering the formatted result of a SQL query as an HTML table; developer controls it via Region, report Attributes, and Column attributes in Page Designer.
workflow: Developer writes a SQL query as region source, then tunes pagination/layout in report Attributes and per-column display in Column Attributes.
skip_for_web: SQL-query-as-source is Oracle-specific; a JS equivalent is an API route returning rows to a generic Table component.

name: Classic Report Appearance: Template and Template Options
apex: The report Template picks the HTML/CSS layout classic report rows render into; the Universal Theme ships many built-in templates beyond a plain table.
attributes: Template: Value Attribute Pairs, Column or Row
Template Options, plus Live Template Options at runtime
workflow: Developer picks a Template, some like Cards or Search Results are row-based and expect specific column aliases from the SQL query, then tunes Template Options for that template look.

name: Classic Report Break Formatting (column breaks)
apex: Suppresses repeated values in a leading column, for example department number, across consecutive rows sharing that value, improving readability of grouped data.
attributes: Break Formatting, Break Columns, consecutive columns from the first displayed column
workflow: Developer sets Break Columns to how many leading columns should collapse repeats for grouped rows.

name: Classic Report Download (CSV/XML export)
apex: Lets end users export the report rows to a file; CSV export is a Download-group toggle, while whole-page XML/CSV export is done by swapping the report Template to a Predefined XML or CSV template.
attributes: Download, Supplemental Text, incompatible with CSV Export Enabled
Appearance, Template Type Predefined plus Template XML or CSV
workflow: Developer enables CSV Export Enabled for an inline download link, or sets Template to a Predefined XML or CSV template to dump the whole page as that file type.

name: Classic Report Column: layout, heading, sort, sum
apex: Common per-column edits: hide it, change its heading text/alignment, reorder it, make it sortable, or total it.
workflow: Developer selects a column under the region Columns node, then edits the matching group; at least one column needs a Default Sequence if any column is sortable.

name: Column Formatting (HTML Expression)
apex: Lets a column render as arbitrary HTML built from other column values via substitution syntax, for badges, colored text, images, or looped lists.
workflow: Developer writes HTML in the HTML Expression field referencing other columns, for example an img tag or a colored span, using loop/if directives for repeated or conditional markup.

name: Column Link (per-column Type: Link)
apex: Turns an ordinary report column into a clickable link to another page or a URL, distinct from the report's special left-hand Link Column.
attributes: Link, Target Type: Page in this application
Clear Cache, Clear/Reset Regions, Reset Pagination
workflow: Developer sets column Type to Link, opens the Link Builder Target dialog, and configures the page/URL target plus session-state and cache-reset behavior.

name: Column visibility (Authorization Scheme, Server-side Condition) and CSV download link
apex: A column can be hidden from unauthorized users or based on a runtime condition; separately, a report can offer a CSV download link independent of its template via Automatic CSV Encoding.
attributes: Automatic CSV Encoding, a Globalization setting
workflow: Developer picks an Authorization Scheme and/or Condition Type on the column; for CSV links, enables Automatic CSV Encoding once so any template with the CSV substitution string offers the link.

name: Filtering on Conditional/Query-built Links (workaround)
apex: A column whose link markup is built inside the SQL query cannot be filtered from the column header menu; the fix is a Hidden raw column paired with a visible HTML Expression alias column for filtering and heading display.
attributes: Identification Type: Hidden, the raw link column
Column Formatting, HTML Expression on a separate display column
Column Filter: custom query on the display column
workflow: Developer adds a second column aliased for display, hides the original link column, and mirrors its heading so the header filter works against readable text, not markup.

name: Interactive Grid Column: heading, type, width
apex: Per-column settings controlling label, how the cell renders or edits, and column width behavior in an interactive grid.
attributes: Heading, Alternative Label for dialogs/Single Row View when heading has HTML
workflow: Developer edits Heading for label/alignment, Type to control render/edit behavior, for example Display Only to lock one column of an otherwise editable grid, and Stretch to override column width auto-sizing.

name: Interactive Report Column Link
apex: Same Link Builder mechanism as classic report columns: sets a column Type to Link and targets a page or URL with optional session-state items and cache reset.
attributes: Link, Target Type: Page in this Application or URL
workflow: Developer sets the column Type to Link then configures the Link Builder Target dialog exactly as for other report types.

name: Interactive Report Column: heading, layout, accessibility, classes
apex: Per-column display and grouping settings for an interactive report column, plus an accessibility hint identifying which column names the row.
attributes: Single Row View, Use Column Heading
List of Values, List of Values
Layout, Group, for Single Row View grouping
workflow: Developer edits these per column; Group clusters columns in the Single Row View popup, and Value Identifies Row names the column that uniquely describes a row for screen readers.

name: Link Column (Interactive Report row-link)
apex: A special left-most column in an interactive report used purely for row navigation; unlike a normal column, it cannot be sorted, hidden, or moved by the end user.
attributes: Link Column: Link to Single Row View
Link Column: Link to Custom Target
Uniquely Identify Rows by: ROWID or Unique Column
workflow: Developer opens the report Attributes tab, Link group, and picks whether the row links to the built-in Single Row View, a custom page/URL target, or nothing.
skip_for_web: Single Row View is a built-in APEX modal; a JS table implements the equivalent as a details drawer or row-click handler.

name: Link Column: Custom Target (page/URL) options
apex: When a Link Column links to a Custom Target, the Link Builder sets the destination page or URL plus session-state and cache-reset behavior for the target.
attributes: Target Type: Page in this Application
Clear/Reset Action: None/Clear Regions/Reset Regions/Reset Pagination
workflow: Developer picks Target Type, and for a page target sets the page number, session-state items to set, and what to clear or reset on arrival.
skip_for_web: Session-state Set Items and page-level cache clearing are APEX-specific server session concepts; a JS link just encodes state as query params or lets the target route refetch.

name: Link Column: Single Row View options
apex: When a Link Column links to Single Row View, extra settings control which columns of the row appear in that built-in detail popup.
workflow: Developer toggles these under the Single Row View group once Link Column is set to Link to Single Row View.

name: Updatable Column and Column as List of Values
apex: A column can be made editable, needs a multirow update process and an updatable SQL Query report type, or rendered from a list of values instead of raw text, useful for showing a lookup label without a SQL join.
attributes: Identification, Type: Plain Text based on List of Values
List of Values, Type: Shared Component
List of Values, Type: SQL Query
List of Values, Type: Static Values
List of Values, Type: PL/SQL Function Body returning SQL Query
workflow: Developer sets the column Type then, for LOV-based types, picks a List of Values Type and supplies its source.
skip_for_web: Multirow update against an Oracle table via a PL/SQL DML process is APEX tabular-form mechanism; a JS grid posts an array of changed rows to an API route instead.

name: Application Computation
apex: A Shared-Components-level computation that sets one page or application item, running at the same point across every page in the app, unlike a page computation scoped to one page.
attributes: Frequency, Computation Point, for example After Submit, On New Instance, After Authentication
workflow: Developer creates it once under Shared Components, Application Computations, rather than per page, typically to compute a value needed on many pages such as tracking the last page visited.
skip_for_web: On New Instance and After Authentication are Oracle-APEX session-lifecycle hooks; a JS app does per-session-start logic in middleware or an auth callback instead.

name: Application Computation: Copy and Subscribe
apex: A shared-component reuse mechanism: an application computation can be copied within or across applications, and a copy can subscribe to its source so future edits to the master propagate to the copy.
workflow: Developer copies a computation from another app and ticks Subscribe to keep it in sync with the master, or later refreshes or unsubscribes from the Subscription region.
skip_for_web: APEX cross-application subscription (one workspace, many apps sharing a component definition) does not map to a single Next.js codebase; the JS equivalent is a shared module imported by multiple pages.

name: Page Computation (points and attributes)
apex: A page computation assigns a value to a page or application item at a specific point during page rendering or processing, independent of validations/processes.
attributes: Execution Options, Point, for example On New Instance or After Submit
workflow: Developer right-clicks Pre-Rendering/Post-Rendering (or Processing) and Create Computation, names the target item, sets Point/Sequence, and picks a Type with its expression.

name: Page Computation Types
apex: The Computation Type decides how the new value is produced: a literal, server logic, a query, or an inline expression.
attributes: SQL Query, return colon separated value
workflow: Developer picks a Type then fills the matching field, referencing other items with ampersand-ITEM-dot or colon-ITEM syntax.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL Function Body and SQL Query types run inside the Oracle DB session; a JS equivalent computes the value in a server function or API route instead.

name: Adding a facet (types, ordering, Synchronize Facets)
apex: A new facet is created by right-clicking Facets and picking a Type; App Builder allows at most one Search-type facet per region, which always renders at the top regardless of its position in the tree.
attributes: Type: Search, max one per region, always shown first
Layout, Sequence, or drag-and-drop, for ordering
Synchronize Facets, context menu action to regenerate facets after table changes
workflow: Developer right-clicks Facets, Create Facet, sets Type, Label and Source column, then orders it with Sequence or drag-and-drop; Synchronize Facets re-runs auto-discovery after the underlying table changes.

name: Auto-Discovered Facets (Data Dictionary Cache)
apex: When a faceted search page is built on a table (not a view or SQL query) via wizard, APEX auto-generates facets by scoring table columns in its Data Dictionary Cache and using the top scoring columns.
attributes: Data Source: View/SQL Query, VARCHAR2-only facet
Data Dictionary Cache refresh: nightly job or manual Gather Statistics/Refresh Cache
workflow: Developer picks a table in the wizard and gets ready made facets for free; switching to a view or SQL query means writing facets manually.
skip_for_web: Relies on Oracle's Data Dictionary Cache and a nightly refresh job; a JS equivalent needs its own schema-introspection heuristic, no direct parallel.

name: Batch Facet Changes
apex: Controls whether picking a facet value filters the report immediately, or stages the change behind an Apply button so several facets can be set before one filter pass.
workflow: Developer enables it on the Faceted Search region when facet changes are expensive or users tend to set several filters at once before wanting results.

name: Cascading facets (Depending On) and inline vs dialog display
apex: One facet options can be scoped to the currently selected value of another facet, and any facet can render inline or tucked behind an Add Filter icon and dialog.
attributes: Depending On, Facet, the parent facet
workflow: Developer picks a parent facet in Depending On so, for example, Assignee only lists people on the selected Project; sets Appearance, Display to Add Filter Dialog to hide a facet.

name: Facet (component attributes)
apex: One filter control inside the Faceted Search region, bound to a single database column or a range on one column.
attributes: Identification, Type: Checkbox Group/Radio Group/Range/Select List/Input Field
Source, Data Type, for Range facets
List of Values, Type: SQL Query/Shared Component/Distinct Values/Static Values
Settings, Select Multiple, for Range facets
workflow: Developer right-clicks Facets, Create Facet, names it, binds it to a column, and picks how its list of values is produced.

name: Facet charts, facet groups, and occurrence counts
apex: Beyond plain filter lists, a faceted search page can show a chart for any facet, group related boolean/flag columns into one facet group, and displays each facet value alongside its result-set occurrence count.
attributes: Facet Groups, for data models with multiple flag columns
occurrence count shown next to each facet value
workflow: Developer toggles a chart type on a facet for a visual filter, or groups several single-purpose flag columns into one combined facet group instead of one facet each.

name: Facet Group (bundling flag columns)
apex: Combines several yes/no database columns, each mapped to its own checkbox, into one compact facet instead of one facet per flag column.
attributes: Checkbox, Settings Checked Value, up to 255 characters
workflow: Developer right-clicks Facets, Create Facet Group, then adds one Checkbox child per flag column, each with its own Database Column and Checked Value.

name: Facet List Entries display (filter box, counts)
apex: Controls shown alongside a facet value list: an inline search box to filter long lists, whether occurrence counts show per value, and whether those counts are computed at all.
attributes: List Entries, Maximum Displayed Entries, filter box hidden below this count
workflow: Developer enables Display Filter Initially on long lists, and turns on Compute Counts and Show Counts so each checkbox shows how many matching rows it would leave.

name: Facet List of Values size limit
apex: A facet list of values, or Distinct Values, is capped at 5000 items; beyond that APEX silently truncates for end users, and raises a developer-only runtime error past 4000, since that many options makes a poor filter UI.
attributes: List of Values / Distinct Values hard cap: 5000 items
workflow: Developer treats a large LOV facet as a design smell and switches that column to a Range, Input Field, or a narrower Distinct Values query instead.

name: Facet on a multi-value column
apex: A single database column that stores several values as one delimited string or JSON array can still drive a Checkbox Group facet, matching rows whose stored list contains a selected value; requires Oracle DB 12.2 or later.
attributes: Multiple Values, Separator, e.g. colon, not double-quote or backslash
Multiple Values, Trim Whitespace, off recommended for performance
Multiple Values, Filter Combination: OR (Union) or AND
List of Values, Include Null Option
List of Values, Null Display Value
workflow: Developer sets Multiple Values Type to Delimited List or JSON Array and a Separator, then picks Filter Combination for how multi-select checks combine.
skip_for_web: Splitting a delimited or JSON column value at query time inside Oracle faceted-search engine is DB-side; a JS equivalent is a normalized join table or a native array-contains query, generally the better design.

name: Facet Types
apex: The Identification, Type attribute on a facet in the Search region picks its input widget; App Builder ships six facet types.
attributes: Checkbox Group: multi-select, stored as one colon-delimited string
Select List: inline dropdown, best for small lists
Range: lower-inclusive/upper-exclusive bands via LOV syntax like 100 pipe 500
Input Field: free-text filter, comparison operator set by developer or end user, supports date/timestamp
Search: a field to search within the facet list itself, one per region
workflow: Developer selects a facet in the Rendering tab and sets Identification, Type; each type then exposes its own extra attributes.

name: Facet vs page item, and region Filtered Region
apex: A facet looks like a page item and follows the same PX_NAME naming convention, but is a distinct component type bound to one report column; most dynamic actions do not apply to facets. The Faceted Search region Filtered Region attribute names the report it controls.
workflow: Developer treats facets as report-bound filter controls, not general-purpose items; wiring is the Filtered Region pointer plus each facet own column binding.

name: Faceted Search Page
apex: A page pattern with a left-side Search region (facets) plus a report region (cards or classic report) showing filtered results, modeled on ecommerce filter UIs.
attributes: Report region: Cards or Classic Report
workflow: Developer builds via Create Application/Page Wizard or manually adds facet plus report region components.

name: Faceted Search Region
apex: The region that holds all facets; it must be told which report region it filters.
attributes: Source, Filtered Region, the target report or cards region
Appearance, Template Options: Remove Body Padding, Header Hidden but accessible
workflow: Developer creates a region, sets Type to Faceted, and points Source/Filtered Region at the already-built classic report or cards region it should filter.

name: Input Field facet settings
apex: An Input Field facet filters a numeric or text column by a typed value and a chosen comparison, and controls how the active filter is labeled once applied.
attributes: Settings, Current Label, uses a percent-0 placeholder for the entered value
workflow: Developer sets Comparison Operator, for example Less than, writes a Current Label template like Less than percent-0, and optional Suffix Text such as a currency or unit label.

name: Range facet static bucket editing and NLS separators
apex: A Range facet static Display Value text can embed locale-aware separator placeholders instead of a hard-coded comma or period, so bucket labels format correctly for every user locale.
attributes: Static Values dialog: Display Value / Return Value per row
substitution hash-G-hash equals NLS Group Separator, e.g. comma
substitution hash-D-hash equals NLS Decimal Separator
workflow: Developer edits Display Value text like 1 hash-G-hash 000 so it renders as 1,000 in the user locale, and edits the matching Return Value range to change the boundary.
skip_for_web: NLS locale substitution is an Oracle globalization feature; a JS app formats numbers with Intl.NumberFormat instead.

name: Range facet static value buckets
apex: For a numeric Range facet with static values, each row defines one bucket as a Display Value label and a Return Value using lower-pipe-upper syntax; an empty side means unbounded.
attributes: Static Values row: Return Value, e.g. pipe1000, 1000pipe3000, 4000pipe
workflow: Developer opens the Static Values dialog and enters one row per bucket, using an empty side of the pipe for open-ended ranges like under 1000 or over 4500.

name: Region layout grid (Sequence, Column, Column Span)
apex: Page Designer arranges sibling regions in a responsive grid; Sequence orders them, Start New Row forces a line break, and Column/Column Span size a region within a grid so a narrow facet panel can sit beside a wider report.
workflow: Developer disables Start New Row on the report region and sets the search region Column Span low, for example 3, so the facet panel and report sit side by side.

name: Reset button (clear all facets)
apex: A button that reloads the current page and resets every region on it back to its default state, clearing all applied facet filters.
attributes: Behavior, Action: Redirect to Page in this Application
Behavior, Target, Page: the current page
Clear/Reset, Clear Cache: the current page
workflow: Developer adds a button targeting its own page, sets Clear Cache to that page number and Action to Reset Regions, giving one-click clearing of all facets and saved state.

name: Search facet across multiple columns
apex: The Faceted Search region auto-creates one search-box item; the developer lists which database columns a typed search term should match against.
attributes: Source, Database Column(s), comma-separated list, e.g. ENAME,JOB,MGR,DEPTNO
workflow: Developer edits the auto-created PX_SEARCH item and enters the comma-delimited column list it should search.

name: Show Total Row Count
apex: Displays how many rows match the current facet filters, either above the facets, wherever the Show Current Facets selector is placed, or at a developer-chosen element via a CSS selector.
attributes: Settings, Show Total Row Count: No
Settings, Show Total Row Count: Yes
Settings, Show Total Row Count: Selector
workflow: Developer sets Yes for the default placement, or Selector plus a target element id to show the count anywhere on the page.

name: Single Facet Charts
apex: Any facet whose counts are computed can show a bar or pie chart of its value counts, either in a popup dialog, hidden entirely, or routed to a developer-placed dashboard element.
attributes: Region Settings, Show Charts: Selector, plus a CSS selector target element
Region Settings, Display Chart for Top N Values
Facet, List Entries, Compute Counts, required for a chart to appear
chart type toggle: bar, default, or pie, at runtime
workflow: Developer turns on Compute Counts for the facet and Show Charts on the region; users open the chart from its context menu and switch bar or pie.

name: Create Page Wizard: Form Data Source and Primary Key
apex: When creating a Form page via the Create Page Wizard, the developer picks where its row comes from and how the row is identified, plus where to branch after submit or cancel.
attributes: Source Type: Table/View or SQL Query
workflow: Developer chooses Component, Form, sets Data Source and Source Type, picks the Primary Key Column, then sets the post-submit and post-cancel branch targets.
skip_for_web: REST Enabled SQL, Duality View and JSON Source are Oracle-specific data-source plumbing; a Next.js form just posts to an API route that knows its own persistence layer.

name: Form (overview and form-type index)
apex: Container topic: developers build forms manually or via wizard; four basic form types are editable interactive grid, form, report with form, master detail; also covers Lost Update Detection and BLOB support.
workflow: Developer picks a form type in the Create Application/Page Wizard based on whether users edit one row, many rows, or master+child rows.

name: Form Types: Editable Interactive Grid
apex: One of the four basic form types: an interactive grid with inline add/edit/delete enabled, used instead of a single-row form when users manage many rows at once.
attributes: Edit, Enabled attribute on existing grid
workflow: Developer enables Editing Enabled in the wizard, or flips Edit/Enabled under Attributes on an existing interactive grid.

name: Form Types: Form (Form on Table)
apex: The basic form type that lets a user update a single row of a database table; Create Page Wizard adds data source choice, breadcrumb/nav menu options, and column selection/order.
attributes: Data source: REST Enabled SQL Service
workflow: Developer runs Create Application Wizard for a quick form, or Create Page Wizard for more control over source and layout.

name: Form Types: Master Detail
apex: A form reflecting a one-to-many relationship between two tables, letting users insert, update and delete master and detail rows together; comes in three layouts.
attributes: Stacked: single page, two editable interactive grids
Side by Side: master list left, selected master detail report right
Drill Down: two pages, master interactive report then standard form plus detail interactive grid
workflow: Developer picks master and detail tables/views and a layout (Stacked/Side by Side/Drill Down) in the wizard.

name: Form Types: Report with Form
apex: An Interactive Report or Classic Report paired with a form page, created by enabling an Include Form flag when building the report so users can drill from a row into an edit form.
attributes: Include Form in Create Application Wizard
Include Form Page in Create Page Wizard
workflow: Developer builds the report first, then turns on the Include Form option so the wizard also generates the linked form page.

name: Lost Update Detection
apex: A form protection that detects when a row was changed by someone else since the form was fetched, and blocks the save with a warning instead of silently overwriting it.
attributes: Lost Update Detection enabled/disabled on the Automatic Row Processing (DML) process
workflow: Enabled by default on a Form region's automatic DML process; developer can disable per-process if not needed.
skip_for_web: Relies on Oracle session-state row versioning; a JS app achieves the same with an updated_at or version column check at the API layer.

name: Master Detail relationship wiring
apex: How the wizard links a master row to its detail rows: composite primary keys on each side plus the foreign key column pair that relates them.
attributes: Show Only Related Tables, restricts the detail-table picklist to FK-related tables
workflow: Developer picks master and detail tables and primary keys, then the foreign key linking them, so the wizard generates the master-detail query and DML.
skip_for_web: Foreign-key-driven wizard inference reads Oracle constraint metadata; a JS app's equivalent is an explicit relation defined in its ORM schema, then hand-wired to the UI.

name: Editable Interactive Grid
apex: An interactive grid whose underlying data users can add to, modify, and refresh directly on the page, not just view; contrasts with a read-only interactive grid.
workflow: Developer sets the grid (and column) Editable attribute; users then add/edit/delete rows inline and save.
skip_for_web: Inline spreadsheet-style bulk editing tied to a DB session is Oracle-specific; a JS app uses per-row edit forms or optimistic UI instead.

name: Interactive Grid (overview)
apex: A searchable, customizable report with the same personalization as Interactive Report plus mouse/keyboard rearrangement, and optional inline editing; users can save Private or Public customized reports.
attributes: Master Detail (two grids from related tables)
workflow: Developer builds the query, sets grid/column attributes, optionally wires a second grid as detail for master-detail; end users reshape via Actions menu at runtime.

name: Interactive Grid Column Filter (LOV Type)
apex: Controls what values populate the filter dropdown or dialog for a column, trading off usability against the cost of computing a list on large columns.
attributes: LOV Type: None, typed partial-match only
LOV Type: Distinct Column, VARCHAR2/NUMBER, DATE/TIMESTAMP get built-in date ranges
LOV Type: PL/SQL Function Body returning SQL Query
LOV Type: Use List of Values
workflow: Developer sets Enabled and picks an LOV Type appropriate to column cardinality; None is recommended for long free-text columns.

name: Interactive Grid Column Link (incl. cross-application target)
apex: Same Link Builder mechanism as other report types, plus an explicit option to target a page in a different application.
attributes: Link, Target Type: Page in this application
Link, Target Type: Page in a different application, plus Application picker
workflow: Developer sets column Type to Link and picks a Target Type, adding an Application selector only when linking cross-app.

name: Interactive Grid Column: Enable Users To (Sort/Hide/Aggregate)
apex: Per-column toggles for which end-user self-service operations are allowed on that column at runtime.
attributes: Enable Users To, Control Break/Aggregate On/Off, requires Sort enabled
workflow: Developer turns these on per column; enabling Sort or Control Break/Aggregate can hurt performance on large unindexed data sets.

name: Interactive Grid Multi Select
apex: Lets users select multiple rows via keyboard, arrow keys, Space, Ctrl+Space, for bulk actions; wiring differs for editable vs read-only grids.
attributes: Editable grid: APEX$ROW_SELECTOR column, Settings, Enable Multi Select Yes/No
workflow: Developer just flips Enable Multi Select on an editable grid auto-created selector column; for a read-only grid it takes hand-written JS.

name: Interactive Grid Region attributes
apex: Region-level settings for an interactive grid: SQL source, region layout/appearance, an optional master-detail link to another region, a region-display selector, and a Server-side Condition for conditional rendering.
workflow: Developer edits the Region tab in the Property Editor to set these; Filter Properties or Go to Group locate a specific attribute.

name: Interactive Grid toolbar and menus (Column Heading, Actions, Row Actions)
apex: Three end-user menus reshape and operate an interactive grid at runtime without developer involvement.
attributes: Column Heading menu: Control Break, Aggregations, Freeze, Hide, Filter
Actions, Format: Control Break/Highlight/Stretch Column Widths
Actions, Selection: Cell Selection/Copy to Clipboard/Refresh Rows
Actions, Report: manage saved Private/Alternative reports
Row Actions menu, editable only: Single Row View/Add Row/Duplicate Row/Delete Row/Refresh Row/Revert Changes
workflow: Developer builds columns and data; end users reshape at runtime via these menus and can save their layout as a Private, Alternative, or Public/Primary report.

name: Interactive Report (overview)
apex: A searchable, end-user customizable report page; users can filter, sort, highlight, define breaks/aggregations/group-bys and their own computations at runtime, beyond what Classic Report allows.
workflow: Developer builds a base SQL query then tunes report/column attributes; end users personalize further via the Actions menu and can save reports.

name: Interactive Report Column Filter (search bar/header filter LOV)
apex: Controls the values offered when an end user filters a column from the column header menu or search bar.
attributes: Column Filter Type: Default Based on Column Type, STRING/NUMBER distinct values, DATE predefined ranges
Column Filter Type: Use Defined List of Values to Filter Exact Match
Column Filter Type: Use Defined List of Values to Filter Word Contains
Column Filter Type: Use Named List of Values to Filter Exact Match
Column Filter Type: Use Named List of Values to Filter Word Contains
workflow: Developer picks a Column Filter Type per column to control what the built-in filter dropdown offers and whether it does exact or contains matching.

name: Interactive Report Region Server-side Condition
apex: A region-level condition (Server-side Condition group, with a Type) controlling whether the interactive report region renders at all; must reference a page item, not colon-REQUEST, because interactive reports refresh via Ajax.
workflow: Developer sets a condition Type in the Region tab; for value based conditions the value must be stashed in a page item, since colon-REQUEST breaks under IR Ajax refresh.

name: Interactive Report Row Selection
apex: Adds a checkbox or radio selector column so users can select one or many rows for a bulk dynamic action or server process; selected primary keys are exposed via a page item.
attributes: Row Selection, Current Selection Page Item, colon-delimited primary keys
workflow: Developer sets a column Type to Row Selector, enables Multi Select and Show Select All, and reads the selection from the Current Selection Page Item or a JS API.

name: Interactive Report toolbar and menus (Column Heading, Actions)
apex: End-user menus for reshaping an interactive report, richer than a grid in Pivot/Group By but with no inline cell editing.
attributes: Column Heading menu: Sort Ascending, Sort Descending, Hide Column, Control Break, Filter
Actions, Format: Control Break/Highlight/Rows Per Page
Actions, Pivot, transpose rows into columns
Actions, Report: manage saved Named reports
workflow: End users personalize columns, filters, and grouping via these menus at runtime and can save the result as a named report; developer just supplies the base query and columns.
skip_for_web: Report-update email Subscription is an Oracle APEX scheduler and mail feature; a JS app would build recurring emails as its own cron job.

name: Report page type trade-offs (Classic vs Interactive Report vs Interactive Grid)
apex: The three tabular report types trade power for simplicity: Classic is template-driven with no scroll paging or frozen columns; Interactive Report adds personalization, Pivot and Group By but no freeze/scroll; Interactive Grid adds inline editing and freeze/scroll but no Pivot, Group By, or computed columns.
attributes: Classic Report: template-driven, Media List/Comments/Timeline/etc, CSV/HTML/Excel/PDF download, PDF Report Layouts, but no scroll/virtual pagination, no column header groups or frozen columns
Interactive Report: Pivot and Group By views, computed columns, complex filters, subscriptions, but no scroll pagination, freeze columns, or column groups
Interactive Grid: inline editing, freeze columns, drag-drop rearrange, but fixed row height, no remembered current page, no Pivot/Group By/computed columns/complex filters
workflow: Developer picks the report type by weighing needed features, editing vs pivoting vs simplicity, against these known gaps before building the page.

name: BOSS REST Data Source Pagination/Total Results
apex: For a REST-backed data source, settings controlling whether total row count is fetched cheaply (Use Total Results) to show '1-20 of 200' without retrieving all rows, and whether paging is supported (Use Pagination).
workflow: Developer sets these when the source is a REST endpoint that may not support paging/counts; APEX adapts its pager display accordingly.
skip_for_web: BOSS REST Data Source config is Oracle-specific plumbing; a Next.js API route just returns {items,total} or a cursor.

name: Classic Report Pagination
apex: Controls how a classic report shows partial result sets and lets users move between pages of rows.
attributes: Pagination, Partial Page Refresh: On updates just the region, Off reloads the whole page
workflow: Developer sets Type and Display Position under the Pagination group in report Attributes; Partial Page Refresh trades a full page reload for an Ajax-only region refresh.

name: Application Process
apex: A Shared-Components-level PL/SQL process that runs at the same point across every page in the app; a special On Demand Process Point lets it be invoked ad hoc from a page or an Ajax call instead of firing automatically.
attributes: Identification, Point, for example On Load: Before Header, On Demand, On New Instance
workflow: Developer creates it once under Shared Components, Application Processes, to avoid repeating the same PL/SQL on every page, for example computing shopping-cart totals shown in a page-zero region.
skip_for_web: On Demand invocation via an f?p= URL keyword and PL/SQL execution are Oracle-APEX specific; a JS equivalent is a shared API route called from any page.

name: Application Process Error Message
apex: Defines what shows the user when a process raises an unhandled exception; for two specific submit-time Points the developer also chooses where that message appears.
attributes: Error message display location: Inline in Notification
Error message display location: On Error Page
workflow: Developer sets the Process Error Message text; for two submit-time Points, also picks Inline in Notification vs On Error Page, using the error page for manually built tabular forms.

name: Page Process (overview)
apex: A page process performs an action at a specified point during page rendering or submission (e.g. after submit); created and edited in Page Designer, can run in foreground or background.
workflow: Developer creates a process under the page's Processing section, picks its point and type; background processing lets a sequence run async.

name: Page Process Types (core data/flow)
apex: The Type chosen for a page process determines what it does and what attributes appear; core types insert/update/delete rows, run code, load or download data, or control flow within the page.
workflow: Developer right-clicks a Rendering/Processing tree node, Create Process, then picks a Type; the Property Editor then shows type specific attributes.
skip_for_web: Execute Code (PL/SQL) and Automatic Row Processing (DML) are Oracle DB transaction specific; a JS API route does inserts/updates directly against its own datastore.

name: Page Process Types (integration/notification/AI/workflow)
apex: Process types that call outside the page: send email or push notifications, call a web service or API, run generative AI, geocode an address, or drive a multi-step Workflow/Human Task.
attributes: Server Side Geocoding, Autonomous DB only
workflow: Developer adds one of these as a page process to integrate with mail, push, REST/SOAP services, or Oracle Workflow/Human Task engine.
skip_for_web: Server Side Geocoding and Workflow/Human Task are Oracle Autonomous DB/APEX engine features with no plain web equivalent; email/push/web-service calls map directly to a Next.js API route or server action.

name: Smart Filters chip-based UI
apex: A more compact alternative to faceted search: one search field up top, filters appear as suggestion chips, and picking a value moves the chip into an Applied Filters area.
attributes: clicking a filter name opens its list of values
clicking an applied chip re-opens its list
workflow: End user clicks a suggested filter chip, picks a value from the list that appears, and the chip moves to Applied Filters; developer configures which columns produce suggestions.

name: Smart Filters Page
apex: A search page with a single search field plus a filter panel, similar to faceted search but simpler; built via wizard or by adding a smart filters region to an existing report.
attributes: Filter region added to existing report
workflow: Developer adds a Smart Filters region on top of an existing report region rather than building a separate facet region.

name: Validation (overview and scope types)
apex: An edit check on user input; scope can be a single page item, an entire page, a single tabular-form column, or a whole tabular-form row. A failed validation blocks all later processes and computations on that submit.
workflow: Developer right-clicks Validations under Processing, Create Validation, names it, picks the Editable Region and Type, then writes the check matching that Type.

name: Validation Error Display
apex: Where and how a failed validation message appears: on a dedicated error page, or inline on the same page either under the associated item label or in the page template notification area.
attributes: Error, Display Location: inline under field label
Error, Display Location: inline in Notification area
workflow: Developer writes the Error Message text, picks Display Location, and for inline picks the Associated Item it attaches to; a hard stop-all error needs the error-page display.

name: Validation Error Message and Display Location
apex: Where a failed validation message renders, chosen from four exact options; the message text can reference the item label or column heading by placeholder.
attributes: Error, Error Message, supports hash-LABEL-hash and hash-COLUMN_HEADER-hash placeholders, not on error page
Display Location: Inline with Field and in Notification
Display Location: On Error Page, required for a hard stop-all error
workflow: Developer writes the Error Message, then picks one of the four Display Location options and, for inline ones, the Associated Item the message attaches under.

name: Validation failure behavior and conditional execution
apex: When any validation fails, APEX redisplays the page with inline errors and skips all Page-Rendering-time computations/processes, such as Automatic Row Fetch, so they do not overwrite what the user typed; a validation can also be scoped with a Server-side Condition or to one button.
attributes: special condition type: Inline Validation Errors Displayed, lets a process still run after a failure
workflow: Developer relies on the skip behavior automatically; to force a process or computation to still run after a failed validation, its Condition Type is set to Inline Validation Errors Displayed.
skip_for_web: Skipping DB row-refetch on validation failure is specific to APEX fetch-then-redisplay page model; a JS form simply keeps the user uncommitted form state in the browser.

name: Validation: Always Execute
apex: A flag deciding if a validation runs regardless of which button submitted the page, or only when the submitting button/item has Execute Validations turned on.
workflow: Developer sets Always Execute On for checks that must never be skipped, such as authorization; otherwise leaves it Off and turns Execute Validations off for buttons like Delete.

name: Wizard-generated validations from column metadata
apex: When a wizard builds a master detail form, it automatically adds validations for columns defined NOT NULL in the table and for NUMBER/DATE/TIMESTAMP-typed columns, skipping any column marked read-only.
attributes: auto-validation skip: column marked read-only, by selection or UI Defaults
workflow: Developer gets these validations for free from the wizard based on table metadata, then can edit or remove them like any other validation afterward.
skip_for_web: Deriving validations from Oracle column constraints and data-dictionary metadata is DB-schema-driven; a JS form generator would derive the same from its schema or ORM types instead.

name: Application Definition - Availability
apex: Whether and to whom the app is currently runnable: fully open, developers-only, restricted to a named user list, or fully unavailable with a custom message or redirect.
attributes: Status (Available/Available with Developer Toolbar/Available to Developers Only/Restricted Access/Unavailable variants)
Build Status (Run and Build Application/Run Application Only)
Restrict to comma separated user list
workflow: Set Status to Restricted Access plus a user list for a soft-launch/beta; set Build Status to Run Application Only when promoting to a production instance to block further edits.
skip_for_web: A single Status toggle backed by the database; a JS site gates the same idea via a feature flag or maintenance-mode middleware plus its own allow-list check.

name: Application Definition - Error Handling
apex: Where validation errors display (inline with the field, in a page-level notification area, or both) and an optional PL/SQL function to rewrite or log an error before it is shown.
workflow: Point Error Handling Function at a PL/SQL function implementing the apex_error package contract to turn a raw DB error into a friendly message or write it to a log table.
skip_for_web: The Error Handling Function is a PL/SQL callback matching the apex_error package signature; a JS app uses a global error boundary or API error middleware instead.

name: Application Definition - Global Notification & Substitutions
apex: Global Notification is one message shown app-wide wherever the page template includes #GLOBAL_NOTIFICATION# (e.g. downtime notices). Substitutions define reusable name/value text pairs referenced as &NAME. everywhere in the app from one place.
workflow: Add the #GLOBAL_NOTIFICATION# token to the page template once, then just edit the Global Notification text to broadcast a banner; define a Substitution String/Value pair once and reuse &NAME. instead of hardcoding a phrase.
skip_for_web: The &NAME. substitution syntax is APEX's template-rendering mechanism; a JS app gets the same reuse from a constants file or i18n dictionary imported wherever needed.

name: Application Definition - Name
apex: Basic identity of the application: its display name, an alphanumeric alias used in friendly URLs, and a version string (optionally auto-derived from the last-modified date).
workflow: Set Application Alias once Friendly URLs is on so the URL shows the alias instead of a numeric app ID; set Version to a YYYY.MM.DD format mask to auto-stamp the last-modified date.

name: Application Definition - Properties
apex: App-wide runtime toggles: URL style, activity logging, debug mode, compatibility with older engine behavior, feedback collection, outbound email from-address, proxy server, and search-query parsing.
workflow: Turn Debugging on only in dev so production users can't see app logic; bump Compatibility Mode only after reading release notes, since it changes runtime behavior app-wide.
skip_for_web: Compatibility Mode (freezing per-release engine behavior), Text Query Function (Oracle Text search operators), and Application Type Library/Boilerplate (shared-component subscription templates) are Oracle-specific with no web-framework equivalent.

name: Application Definition - Workflow, Printing, File Storage, Copyright
apex: Secondary app-wide settings: a vacation-rule procedure for task workflows, which print server renders PDF/RTF/XLS reports, whether Static Application Files live in the database or Oracle Cloud Object Storage, and copyright text embedded in exports.
attributes: Report Printing (Native/Remote Print Server/Use Instance Settings)
File Storage Type (Database/Oracle Cloud Object Storage)
workflow: Switch File Storage Type to Oracle Cloud Object Storage plus a Remote File Server when static files need to live outside the database.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL vacation-rule procedures, native PDF/RTF/XLS report servers, and OCI Object Storage wiring are Oracle-specific; a JS app stores assets in its own bucket/CDN and generates PDFs with a JS/server library.

name: Globalization Attributes
apex: App-wide i18n/l10n settings: the source language all translations derive from, how translation is implemented, text direction, date/time/timestamp format masks, locale-aware string sorting, browser-derived time zone, and CSV export encoding.
workflow: For one app supporting several languages without duplicate pages, turn on Translate Application with Translate Method = Text Message-Based, then store every UI string as a Text Message referenced via &{NAME}.
skip_for_web: Application-Based translation (a whole cloned app per language) and NLS_* database-session parameters are Oracle-specific; a JS app uses one codebase with an i18n library and the browser's Intl API instead.

name: PWA: General & Installability
apex: Turns the app into an installable PWA (home-screen icon) and declares its manifest-equivalent look: display chrome, orientation, theme/background color, iOS status-bar style, an install-prompt description, promotional screenshots, and a Custom Manifest JSON block to add or override raw manifest properties.
workflow: Enable Progressive Web App then Installable; fill Display/Theme Color/Background Color/Screenshots to control the install-prompt, like hand-authoring a Web App Manifest.
skip_for_web: Only unlocks when Friendly URLs is On. A hand-built Next.js PWA just ships its own manifest.json and Serwist config directly, with no such gating.

name: PWA: Service Worker Configuration
apex: Controls the generated service worker: Default installs a cache-then-network-then-offline-page strategy automatically; Configure Hooks fills in placeholders in APEX's generated worker code; File URL points at an externally hosted hooks file to share one worker across apps.
workflow: Start with Default; move to Configure Hooks only when custom fetch/notification handling is needed.
skip_for_web: Paddock already hand-rolls its own service worker via @serwist/next; APEX's hook-placeholder model is a declarative alternative to writing the worker script directly.

name: PWA: Shortcuts & Push Notifications
apex: Shortcuts are long-press/right-click jump links to specific pages from the installed app's icon (needs Rejoin Sessions on). Push Notifications lets installed users subscribe to web push, using a stored public/private key Credential and a Contact Email for the push provider.
workflow: Click Add Shortcut per quick-access page; enable Push Notifications and pick a Credential to add a User Settings nav entry for subscribing.
skip_for_web: The public/private key Credential maps onto the standard Web Push API; a hand-coded PWA implements the same subscribe/send flow in its own service worker instead of APEX's declarative wiring.

name: User Interface: Attributes (misc)
apex: App-wide UI defaults: whether users can pick their own Theme Style, an auto-dismiss timer for success toasts, the Home/Login page targets, current Theme, and an optional Global Page whose components render on every page.
attributes: Enable End Users to choose Theme Style
Add Built with APEX to Footer
workflow: Set a Global Page to place components (e.g. a persistent alert) on every page without adding them individually to each page.
skip_for_web: Global Page as an APEX region-inheritance mechanism is theme-specific; a JS app gets the same effect from a shared layout component wrapping every route.

name: User Interface: Concatenated Files & Advanced
apex: Concatenated Files merge many small JS/CSS files into one to cut HTTP requests; #APP_FILES#/#APEX_FILES# Path override where static/app-builder-image assets are served from (e.g. a CDN); Media Type sets the page's Content-Type header.
workflow: Point #APP_FILES# Path at a CDN URL to serve static application files from outside the database for performance.
skip_for_web: Concatenating files into one bundle is what a JS build tool (webpack/Vite) already does automatically; the #APP_FILES#/#APEX_FILES# indirection is APEX's own asset-serving mechanism.

name: User Interface: Icon & Logo
apex: App Icon: one upload auto-resizes into Favicon, PWA icon, Apple touch icon and App Builder icon at 5 fixed sizes. Logo: choose None/Image/Text/Image and Text/Custom to fill the page template's #LOGO# slot in the top nav bar.
workflow: Upload once via Change Icon; for Logo, pick a type - the page template must include #LOGO# for it to render.

name: User Interface: JavaScript & CSS File URLs
apex: Lists of external JS/CSS file URLs (one per line) loaded on every page, substituting into the page template's #APPLICATION_JAVASCRIPT#/#APPLICATION_CSS# slots; #MIN#/#MIN_DIRECTORY# tokens swap in a minified file outside debug mode, #APP_VERSION# cache-busts CSS.
attributes: Include Deprecated or Desupported Javascript Functions
workflow: Add a CDN or app-file URL per line; use [require requirejs]/path or [media="..."]/path prefixes for RequireJS dependencies or responsive media-query CSS.
skip_for_web: jQuery Migrate and RequireJS-specific URL prefixes are legacy-APEX-runtime concerns; a modern JS bundler handles minification, versioning and conditional loading natively.

name: Automation
apex: A scheduled or programmatically-triggered background job: runs a query, then executes a sequence of actions (usually PL/SQL) once per result row (or once if the query returns none), with each row's columns available as bind variables.
attributes: Data Source (local database/REST Enabled SQL/REST Data Source)
workflow: Define the query and schedule, add ordered Actions that fire per row when their Condition passes, set Error Handling so one bad row can't silently break the whole run; trigger ad hoc via APEX_AUTOMATION from other PL/SQL.
skip_for_web: Automations are PL/SQL-first background jobs run by an Oracle scheduler coordinator inside the database (needs CREATE JOB privilege); a JS app's equivalent is a cron-triggered serverless function or queue worker calling its own API/DB directly.

name: Automation Execution Log & History
apex: Every automation run is recorded (per-row outcomes and messages) in an Execution Log that can be reviewed or cleared; a separate History report tracks changes made to automation definitions over time.
workflow: After an automation misbehaves, check its Execution Log and Log Messages first to see which rows failed and why, before touching the automation's actions.

name: Automation Import/Export behavior
apex: After an application containing automations is imported into a new environment, every automation is disabled by default and must be manually re-enabled before it will run.
workflow: After any app import/deploy that includes automations, check Shared Components, Automations and re-enable each one that should be active in the new environment.
skip_for_web: Import-disables-automations is an APEX deployment safety default; a JS app's scheduled jobs are defined in code/infra config and run automatically whenever that code deploys, with no separate disabled state to remember.

name: Automation Scheduling mechanics
apex: A background coordinator job checks for due automations at regular intervals, so the actual run happens up to a few minutes after the Next Execution Due time shown on the automation's edit page, not exactly at it.
workflow: Don't rely on an automation's Next Execution Due timestamp for precise timing; expect a few minutes of coordinator-job lag, and confirm the CREATE JOB privilege is granted to the app's parsing schema or scheduled automations silently never run.
skip_for_web: The CREATE JOB privilege and Oracle Scheduler coordinator job are database-level prerequisites; a JS app's cron/queue scheduler has its own (usually simpler) permission model.

name: Email Template
apex: A reusable HTML + Plain Text email layout with named #PLACEHOLDER# tokens filled at send time; placeholders auto-escape by context (HTML-escaped in HTML format, none in Plain Text) unless overridden with !RAW or !STRIPHTML modifiers.
workflow: Define the template once, then send it via a page button's Send E-Mail process (pick the template, fill Placeholder Values from page/app items) or from PL/SQL with apex_mail.send(p_template_static_id, p_placeholders) plus apex_mail.push_queue.
skip_for_web: apex_mail.send/push_queue is Oracle APEX's built-in mail-merge and send-queue API; a JS app sends templated email via its own provider SDK (Resend/SendGrid/Postmark) with a similar named-placeholder template.

name: Email Template Reports & Sample Templates
apex: APEX ships three ready-made sample templates (Load Order Details, Load Event Reminder, Load Scheduled Outage) a developer can load as a starting point; a Utilization report shows where each template is used and a History report tracks recent edits.
attributes: Sample Templates (Load Order Details/Load Event Reminder/Load Scheduled Outage)
workflow: Start a new template from the closest sample instead of writing HTML email markup from scratch.

name: Breadcrumb Entry
apex: One node in a breadcrumb's hierarchy: the page it points to, its parent entry, and its label text; the template renders the chain from root down to the current entry.
attributes: Target is a (Page in this Application/URL)
workflow: Click New Entry under a breadcrumb; set the target page or URL and the parent entry to build the tree; exactly one root entry (no parent) per breadcrumb.
skip_for_web: Clear Cache / Set session state and the REQUEST item are Oracle page-submission (f?p=) mechanics; a stateless JS route has no equivalent.

name: Breadcrumb Region & Template
apex: The breadcrumb's on-page rendering settings: Region attributes for the container plus breadcrumb-specific Attributes (Breadcrumb Template, Template Options, CSS Classes) controlling layout/style of the crumb trail.
workflow: In Page Designer select the region holding the breadcrumb; edit its Region tab and Attributes tab separately; reparent entries by drag-and-drop or right-click Reparent; clear orphaned entries from the Utilization tab's Delete Unused.

name: Breadcrumb Reports
apex: The Breadcrumbs page in Shared Components exposes Grid Edit (bulk-edit all entries in a spreadsheet-like view), Utilization (where entries are used/orphaned), and History (recent changes) as separate report tabs.
workflow: Use Grid Edit to bulk-adjust sequence/labels across many breadcrumb entries at once instead of opening each entry individually.

name: Breadcrumbs
apex: Hierarchical list of links showing where the user is in the app hierarchy; usually placed via the Title Bar region template, gives a path back to Home.
workflow: Create in Shared Components or Page Designer, add entries under it, then add a Breadcrumb region to a page and select the breadcrumb as its source.

name: Dynamic Breadcrumb Labels
apex: A breadcrumb entry's Short Name or Long Name can embed a session-state substitution such as &COMPANY_NAME. so the crumb shows runtime data, e.g. Home > Orders > Orders for ACME Inc.
workflow: Type the item's substitution syntax directly into the Short Name/Long Name field of a breadcrumb entry.
skip_for_web: Relies on Oracle's &ITEM. session-state substitution; a JS app just interpolates a variable/prop into the label string.

name: Attribute Dictionary
apex: A reusable, name-matched (or synonym-matched) set of default attributes for a column (label, format, LOV) that can push its values onto every page item/report column sharing that column name, or pull a page's current values back into the dictionary.
workflow: Define an attribute once for a column name (e.g. EMAIL), then use Manage Attribute Dictionary to bulk-apply it to every item/report column named EMAIL across the app instead of setting each one by hand.
skip_for_web: Matching by database column name/synonym across forms and reports is an APEX low-code-generation concept; a JS design system gets the same consistency from a shared field-config object keyed by field name.

name: Component Settings (concept)
apex: One app-level settings panel per built-in item type or installed plug-in, letting a developer set defaults that apply everywhere that component is used (e.g. default checked value, avatar images, geocoding strictness) instead of repeating them on every instance.
workflow: Shared Components, Component Settings, pick the component name, edit its settings, Apply Changes; a History report tracks recent changes across all component settings.
skip_for_web: Applies to built-in APEX item types and Oracle integrations (BOSS/SaaS REST, server-side geocoding); a component library gives a JS app the same 'set once, apply everywhere' effect via shared defaultProps/design tokens.

name: Component Settings: Checkbox & Color Picker
apex: Checkbox sets the two stored values for a checkbox item's checked/unchecked states app-wide; Color Picker sets how the color-input control displays (popup, inline, button-triggered popup, or the browser's native picker) and how much detail (hex/HSL/RGB, presets) it exposes.
workflow: Set Unchecked Value blank to store NULL instead of a literal 'N' when a checkbox is cleared.

name: Component Settings: Date Picker
apex: App-wide defaults for every Date Picker item's calendar popup: which navigation aids show, how out-of-month days behave, the time-selector increment, and whether the popup opens on focus or only on icon click.
workflow: Set once here instead of repeating the same calendar behavior on every Date Picker item in the app.

name: Component Settings: Geocoded Address & Server Side Geocoding
apex: App-wide defaults for turning a postal address into map coordinates: how loosely an input address may match known data, how results display, and whether/where a map preview shows.
