attributes: Geocoder Match Mode (Exact/Relax Street Type/Relax House Number/Relax Street Name/Relax Postal Code/Relax All)
workflow: Loosen Match Mode from Exact toward Relax All when real-world address data is messy (e.g. race-venue addresses from varied sources) and too many lookups fail to match.
skip_for_web: Server-side geocoding with graduated match-relaxation is an Oracle Maps Cloud Service feature; a JS app calls a geocoding API (Google/Mapbox/OpenStreetMap Nominatim) directly and implements its own fallback/fuzzy-match logic.

name: Component Settings: Interactive Report Action Menu & Select Many
apex: Interactive Report setting picks whether the report's Actions menu uses the newer Interactive-Grid-style structure or the Legacy layout; Select Many sets how a multi-value item displays its chosen values when not focused.
workflow: Switch Actions Menu Structure to Interactive Grid to give older interactive reports the same Actions menu users already know from interactive grids.

name: Component Settings: Oracle Cloud Applications REST integrations
apex: App-level configuration for two Oracle SaaS integration types: BOSS REST Service accepts advanced setting names (support-guided) and the SaaS REST Service accepts a metadata sandbox name so App Builder and runtime work against in-progress customizations instead of only published ones.
workflow: Set Sandbox Name when developing against Oracle SaaS customizations that haven't been published yet.
skip_for_web: Both settings are specific to consuming Oracle Cloud Applications (Fusion/SaaS) REST endpoints; irrelevant outside that Oracle ecosystem.

name: Component Settings: Show AI Assistant
apex: App-wide default avatars for the built-in AI chat assistant plug-in: how the AI's and the current user's avatar are rendered (a default icon, a custom icon class, an image URL, or initials).
workflow: Set once so every page using the Show AI Assistant action displays consistent branding without repeating avatar config per instance.

name: Component Settings: Star Rating & Region Display Selector/Maps
apex: Star Rating sets the default icon and active/inactive colors plus a hover tooltip template for every star-rating item; Region Display Selector auto-adds a slider when a region-name tab overflows its width; Maps can switch background tiles to higher-resolution Vector Tile Layers.
workflow: Set a Tooltip template like 'rating is #VALUE#' once so every Star Rating item gets a consistent accessible hover label.

name: Component Settings: Switch
apex: App-wide default look and stored values for every Switch item: render as a toggle, pill button, or select list, and what value/label represents On vs Off.
workflow: Change Display Style once to restyle every Switch item app-wide without touching individual pages.

name: JSON Source
apex: Exposes a database table's JSON column(s), or a native JSON Collection Table, as row/column data for APEX components, by inferring or importing a Data Profile that maps JSON attributes to typed columns.
attributes: JSON Source Type (JSON Collection Table/Table with JSON columns)
Data Profile (Row Selector, Columns, Primary Key per level)
workflow: Point at a table plus its JSON column(s); let APEX sample existing rows to infer the Data Profile, or upload a JSON Schema file when there is little sample data; use the result as a region/LOV/automation data source.
skip_for_web: JSON Collection Tables and Data-Profile inference from a JSON Schema are Oracle-Database-specific; a JS app just JSON.parse()s the stored/fetched document directly, no separate profile object.

name: JSON Source data constraints
apex: Plain tables with JSON columns work on Oracle Database 19c/21c; native JSON Collection Tables need Oracle AI Database 26ai or later; a JSON Schema used to seed the Data Profile must be one self-contained file (no imports/refs, $id ignored).
workflow: Upload a JSON Schema instead of relying on sample-data inference when the source table is empty or its existing rows aren't representative.
skip_for_web: Version-gated Oracle Database JSON storage features (Collection Tables, in-DB JSON Schema parsing) are Oracle-specific; a JS app validates JSON with any standard schema library (e.g. Zod, Ajv) regardless of database version.

name: REST Data Source
apex: A named external HTTP/JSON/XML API definition a region, chart, or calendar can read from like a table; a Data Profile tells APEX which response attribute holds the row array and how to map each attribute to a typed column, including nested Array Columns for JSON.
attributes: REST Data Source Type (Simple HTTP/Oracle REST Data Services/REST Enabled SQL Query/Oracle Cloud SaaS/OCI/OData/BOSS)
Operations (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE mapped to a Database Action)
Data Profile (Response Format, Row Selector, Array Columns, Columns)
workflow: Pick the closest built-in Type, define Operations and their Database Action, let APEX auto-discover the Data Profile from a sample response, then use it as a region's Source Type instead of a SQL query.
skip_for_web: This is APEX's declarative alternative to writing a fetch() call and parsing JSON by hand; a JS app calls the REST API directly in a server component/API route and shapes the response with plain code.

name: REST Data Source Credential
apex: A named, reusable Authentication method plus Client ID/Client Secret pair stored once in Shared Components and attached to a Remote Server or a specific REST Data Source; a credential set at the Data-Source level overrides one inherited from its Remote Server.
workflow: Store one Credential per external service and reuse it across every REST Data Source that talks to that service, instead of re-entering secrets per source.
skip_for_web: Encrypted, write-only Credential storage shared across Remote Servers/REST Data Sources is APEX's own secrets vault; a JS app keeps the equivalent secret in an environment variable or a secrets manager (e.g. Cloudflare/Vercel env vars).

name: REST Data Source Data Profile details
apex: The Data Profile's Response Format is JSON, XML, or CSV; XML/CSV are always treated as one flat table, while JSON alone supports nested Array Columns (a row-set inside a row-set), and a column can never reference an Array Column that is its own child or grandchild.
workflow: For a nested JSON response (e.g. an order with a line-items array), define the line items as an Array Column so a component can pick that array as its own row source.

name: REST Data Source Operations vs Legacy Web Services
apex: Unlike a Legacy Web Service Reference, a REST Data Source stores metadata APEX components can use directly; each Operation (GET/PUT/POST/DELETE) is assigned exactly one Database Action (Fetch Multiple Rows/Fetch Single Row/Insert Row/Update Row/Delete Row), letting a region treat the REST endpoint like an editable table.
attributes: Database Action (Fetch Multiple Rows/Fetch Single Row/Insert Row/Update Row/Delete Row)
workflow: Map each REST endpoint verb to the Database Action a region needs (e.g. GET to Fetch Multiple Rows) so a report or form region can read and write through the same Data Source.
skip_for_web: Mapping HTTP verbs to a fixed CRUD vocabulary so generic report/form regions can bind to them is an APEX low-code convenience; a JS app calls each endpoint explicitly in its own data-fetching code.

name: REST Data Source structure (Source vs Operations)
apex: One REST Data Source can contain many Operations, each a reference to one concrete external web-service call; configuration set at the Source level (such as authentication or the base endpoint) is shared across every Operation it contains rather than repeated per-call.
workflow: Configure authentication once on the REST Data Source, then add one Operation per endpoint/verb it exposes (list, get-one, create, update, delete) without re-entering credentials each time.

name: Actions: Component & Navigation
apex: Actions that manipulate page components or navigation: toggle visibility/editability, push a value into an item, move focus, refresh a report/region, open/close inline dialogs or tree nodes, submit the page, cancel a dialog/event.
workflow: Pick the action type on a True/False Action row, choose its Affected Elements (target component(s)), then set type-specific options such as Set Value's value source.

name: Actions: Execute, Style & Notification
apex: Actions that run code, restyle elements, message the user, or call generative AI: Execute JS/PL-SQL, add/remove a CSS class or set a style property, show Alert/Confirm dialogs or success/error banners, invoke a configured AI service.
workflow: Execute Server-side Code runs PL/SQL on submit (enable Show Processing for a spinner on long calls); Confirm pauses the chain until the user responds, canceling remaining actions on Cancel.
skip_for_web: Execute Server-side Code and Generate Text With AI (Oracle's configured Generative AI Service) are Oracle-hosted; a JS app calls its own backend endpoint or LLM API directly instead.

name: Actions: Miscellaneous, AI extras & Report Dialog
apex: Less-common action types rounding out the catalogue: trigger the browser's geolocation prompt, share the current page/URL/files via the OS share sheet, re-run address geocoding, or pop the Interactive Report customization dialog (columns/filters/highlights).
workflow: Use Get Current Position plus Set Value to capture a user's location into a page item; use Invoke Interactive Report Dialog to open the same customize-report UI a user gets from the report's own menu, from a custom button.
skip_for_web: Get Current Position/Share map directly onto the browser's Geolocation and Web Share APIs a JS app already calls directly; no APEX-specific gap here.

name: Calling JavaScript from a Dynamic Action
apex: Custom JS enters two ways: an Execute JavaScript Code action (or a Set Value sourced from JS), or a Client-side Condition of type JavaScript Expression returning true/false to pick the True/False branch.
workflow: Use the page-level Function and Global Variable Declaration attribute for JS reused across several actions on one page, then call those functions from an Execute JavaScript Code action.

name: Debugging Dynamic Actions
apex: Dynamic action firing is logged to the browser's JavaScript console (not server logs) as 'Dynamic Action Fired: [DA name] ([Action name]) {details}', visible once the app's Debug mode is on.
attributes: Enable Debug: No Debug/Info/App Trace/Full Trace
workflow: Turn on Debug from the Developer toolbar, open the browser console, run/reload the page, and watch for the Dynamic Action Fired log line to confirm a DA actually triggered.
skip_for_web: This is literally browser-devtools console output; a JS app already gets richer debugging for free from devtools/breakpoints without a special app debug mode.

name: Dynamic Action
apex: Declarative client-side behavior: a Trigger (an event plus optional condition on a component) paired with Actions (True/False) that run without hand-written JavaScript; more DAs on a page means more emitted client code to download.
workflow: Pick or create the triggering component (item, button, region), add a dynamic action defining the event and the actions to run, then run the page to test.

name: Dynamic Action - Action attributes
apex: Settings on each True/False Action row: its name, which Action type to run, which elements it targets, its own sequence/event, whether it runs on the True or False branch, and whether it also fires once on page load or grid-row-edit start.
workflow: Right-click the dynamic action, Create TRUE Action or Create FALSE Action; pick the Action type and Affected Elements; enable Fire on Initialization to also run once when the page loads (or when a grid row starts editing).

name: Dynamic Action attributes (the trigger)
apex: Top-level settings on a dynamic action: its name, execution order, which event fires it, what page element triggers it, and an optional client-side condition gating True vs False actions.
workflow: Right-click Events in the Dynamic Actions tab, Create Dynamic Action; set Event (e.g. Change) and Selection Type (e.g. Item) as the trigger; set Client-side Condition Type (e.g. Item = Value) so True/False actions diverge.

name: Dynamic Action Event Scope & Execution Type
apex: How re-fireable the trigger is: Event Scope (Static=unbound after Partial Page Refresh recreates the element, Dynamic=survives PPR via a stable container selector, Once=fires only until full reload) and execution Type (Immediate/Debounce/Throttle) to rate-limit rapid events.
workflow: Use Dynamic scope plus a Static Container selector when the triggering element gets replaced by AJAX refresh; use Debounce for 'wait until typing stops', Throttle for 'update at most every N seconds'.
skip_for_web: Partial Page Refresh rebinding is an artifact of APEX's server-rendered-then-AJAX-patched DOM; a React/Vue app's event bindings survive re-renders automatically via the framework's own diffing.

name: Dynamic Action Events
apex: The trigger half of a dynamic action: what must happen to fire it. Four categories: Browser events (native DOM events), Framework events (Page Load, Before/After Refresh, Dialog Closed), Component events (custom events from native/plug-in components), and Custom (developer-named).
attributes: Dialog Closed / Dialog Closed or Canceled
workflow: Choose an Event on the dynamic action, e.g. Change on a page item, Click on a button, Page Load on a region; Custom lets you name a bespoke JS-fired event.

name: Developer Comments
apex: A free-text Comments field attached to most shared components and pages, for internal notes to other developers; separate from Team Development's issue-tracking comments.
workflow: Type notes in a component's Comments attribute (e.g. a List, Build Option, or via Shared Components, Developer Comments) so other developers see context without touching functionality.

name: Static Application Files
apex: App-scoped static assets (images, CSS, JS) uploaded once and referenced via the #APP_FILES# substitution string; can live in the database or, for performance, an external OCI Object Storage bucket.
attributes: File Storage Type (Database/Oracle Cloud Object Storage)
workflow: Upload a file under Shared Components, Static Application Files, then reference it as #APP_FILES#myfile.css in templates, a region source, or the JS/CSS File URLs attribute.
skip_for_web: Storing static assets inside database rows is an APEX-specific pattern; a JS app puts files in its own public/ folder or a CDN/object-storage bucket and references them by URL.

name: Static Application Files vs Static Workspace Files
apex: Static Application Files are scoped to one application; Static Workspace Files (images, CSS, other assets) live at the workspace level and are therefore available to every application in that workspace.
workflow: Put an asset in Static Workspace Files only when several apps in the same workspace need to share it; otherwise keep it app-scoped to avoid cross-app coupling.
skip_for_web: Workspace-level shared file storage across multiple APEX apps has no direct equivalent in a single-app JS project; the nearest analogue is a shared package/CDN bucket used by multiple projects.

name: Team Development Issue Comments
apex: APEX's built-in project-tracking feature: developers add threaded comments (with a Response Template, rich-text formatting, file attachments) to a tracked Issue, then close/hide/edit them.
workflow: Open an issue under Team Development, scroll to Add Comment, write/format the note, optionally attach a file, then click Comment or Comment and Close.
skip_for_web: This is Oracle APEX's own bundled issue-tracker for the development team, unrelated to any end-user-facing feature; a web project would use GitHub/Linear/Jira instead.

name: Dynamic List Query Contract
apex: A dynamic list's SQL/PL-SQL query returns columns by fixed position, not alias: Level, Label, Target URL, Is Current, Icon Name, Image attrs, Image Alt, then up to 10 User Attributes (e.g. badge text). 2-17 columns; unused ones are NULL.
attributes: Query Source Type (SQL Query/Function Returning SQL Query)
workflow: Write a SELECT with columns in that exact order, e.g. return salary as User Attribute 1 to show as badge text when the list template is Badge List; CONNECT BY on the Level column builds a hierarchy.
skip_for_web: Entirely Oracle SQL/PL-SQL driven (CONNECT BY hierarchy queries, positional column contract); a JS equivalent just maps an API/DB result array to nav objects in code.

name: Hierarchical (Sublist) Lists
apex: A list can nest sublists: pick a list template whose 'List Template Current with Sublist Items' attribute is set, then give each child entry a Parent List Entry to build the tree.
workflow: Choose a template named '...with Sublist', then set Parent List Entry per child entry; reparent later via drag-and-drop or the dedicated Reparent page.
skip_for_web: Template-driven sublist rendering is an APEX theming mechanic; a JS component tree just nests a recursive nav component from a plain data structure.

name: List Entry Click Counting
apex: A static list entry that links to an external page can optionally count how many times it was clicked, tagged with a category, via the built-in COUNT_CLICK procedure.
workflow: Enable Count Clicks on outbound navigation links to see which external destinations users actually follow.
skip_for_web: COUNT_CLICK is an Oracle APEX PL/SQL API writing to an APEX-internal table; a JS site tracks link clicks with its own analytics event (e.g. a client-side analytics call) instead.

name: List management & reports
apex: Shared Components tooling for lists: copy or subscribe to a list from another app, and reports (Unused, Conditional Entries, Utilization, History, Grid Edit) for auditing all entries across a list.
workflow: From the Lists page in Shared Components, use Copy List / Subscribe to List, or open a list's report tabs to review usage before cleanup.

name: List Region
apex: The page region that renders a chosen list: region type List, a Source list to render, plus layout, template, and optional condition/authorization on the whole region.
workflow: Drag a List region onto a page, pick the list as its Source, choose a template, save.

name: List Subscription (shared component pattern)
apex: A list can subscribe to a 'master' list, often defined in a different application; Apply Changes pulls a copy of the master's details in, Refresh List re-syncs later master edits.
workflow: Set Subscribe From to a master list to copy its definition in; click Refresh List after the master changes to pull updates.
skip_for_web: Cross-application component subscription/sync is an APEX workspace concept; a JS site would just share a navigation config module/import across pages.

name: Lists as Navigation
apex: A list is a shared, reusable collection of links; adding a List region to a page and choosing a list template turns it into a navigation menu (side/top) or navigation bar.
workflow: Create a list once in Shared Components, then add a List region to any page and pick a list template to control how it renders.

name: Navigation Bar (list-based)
apex: A small list of links/icons rendered in the #NAVIGATION_BAR# page-template slot (typically top-right), e.g. account/help/notifications; can be List-based or the older Classic style.
workflow: In Shared Components, User Interface Attributes, set Implementation to List, choose the list and its List Template; edit the list itself like any other list.

name: Navigation Menu
apex: The app's primary hierarchical navigation list, auto-created by the Create Application Wizard with one entry per page; renders as Side Menu (collapsible tree), Top Menu (tabs or menu bar), or Mega Menu (popup panel).
workflow: Edit Application Definition, User Interface tab, Navigation Menu section; choose Side or Top position and a matching List Template (Top Navigation Tabs for <=6 items, Top Navigation Menu or Mega Menu for deeper hierarchies).
skip_for_web: Auto-generated per-page nav list and theme-level Side/Top/Mega positioning are Universal Theme specifics; a JS app defines nav as an explicit config/array rendered by a layout component.

name: Static List Entry
apex: One link/item within a static list: its label, icon, click target, hierarchy position, and the rule for when it counts as 'current' (highlighted as active) so templates can render it distinctly.
attributes: List Entry Current for Pages Type
workflow: Click Create Entry on the List Details page; set label/icon/target; set Parent List Entry to nest under another entry for a sublist; define current-page rules so the active nav item highlights.
skip_for_web: Target session-state fields (Request, Clear Cache, Set these items/With these values) are Oracle page-submission concepts; a JS router just needs a route path plus active-link matching.

name: Static List vs Dynamic List
apex: Static lists have hand-entered fixed entries (label + target); dynamic lists are generated at runtime from a SQL query or PL/SQL function, e.g. one entry per row.
workflow: Choose static for fixed/manually curated navigation; choose dynamic when entries should be generated from data.
skip_for_web: Dynamic lists driven by SQL/PL-SQL are Oracle-DB-specific; a JS site would map nav entries from a JSON/config array or CMS query instead.

name: Switching from Tabs to Navigation Menus
apex: An app built on an older tabs-based theme can switch to a navigation-menu theme only if it currently uses one level of tabs; two levels of tabs must first be collapsed to one before the theme switch.
workflow: Flatten a parent-tab/standard-tab hierarchy to a single level before changing the application's theme to one that uses Navigation Menus.
skip_for_web: Tabs vs Navigation Menu is a Universal-Theme-generation migration path; a JS app just swaps which nav component it renders, no such one-level constraint.

name: Attaching an Authorization Scheme
apex: The same Authorization Scheme picklist appears at three levels: Security Attributes (whole app), a page's root Property Editor (one page), and any individual region/item/button/list entry/tab's Security section (just that control).
workflow: Set at the narrowest level that matches the rule: app-level for 'must be logged in everywhere', page-level for an admin-only page, component-level for a single admin-only button.
skip_for_web: Run on Background Job's cloned-session-state caveat is specific to APEX's interactive-report-subscription background jobs; a JS app's background jobs read straight from its real database/session store.

name: Authentication (concept)
apex: Establishes who the user is (vs Authorization, which checks what they may do); once authenticated, APP_USER identifies the user for the rest of the session and can gate any page or control's display.
workflow: Choose no-authentication, a built-in scheme, or a custom PL/SQL function run before every page request; enable Deep Linking so an out-of-context link lands on the actual target page after sign-in instead of Home.
skip_for_web: Paddock uses Clerk for authentication, so APEX's Authentication Scheme types (built-in/custom PL/SQL) do not apply; Clerk's middleware plus its own redirect-after-sign-in already covers deep linking.

name: Authorization Scheme
apex: A named pass/fail security check attachable to an application, page, or any control (region, item, button, list entry, tab); if it fails, the control is hidden/disabled or, at app/page level, an error message displays instead.
attributes: Identify error message displayed when scheme violated
workflow: Create one scheme per access rule (e.g. Is In Group = ADMIN), then pick it from any component's Security, Authorization Scheme property; the result can be cached for the session instead of re-evaluated every use.

name: Authorization Scheme Reports
apex: Two reports help manage authorization schemes app-wide: a Subscription report (schemes copied/subscribed from elsewhere) and a Utilization report (every component a given scheme is attached to).
workflow: Check the Utilization report before editing or removing a shared authorization scheme, to see everything that would be affected.

name: Authorization Scheme Types
apex: The pass/fail logic behind a scheme: a SQL existence check, a custom PL/SQL boolean function, a null-check or exact-match on an item's or preference's value, or membership in a role/group.
attributes: Item in Expression 1 is NULL / is NOT NULL
Value of Item Equals/Does NOT Equal Expression 2
Value of Preference Equals/Does NOT Equal Expression 2
workflow: Pick Is In Group for role-based UI gating; pick PL/SQL Function Returning Boolean for anything more complex than the built-in comparison types.
skip_for_web: Exists/NOT Exists SQL Query and PL/SQL Function Returning Boolean run as database queries/procedures; a JS app runs the equivalent check in its own API route or middleware against its own DB/session claims.

name: Security: Advanced (Runtime API / ECID)
apex: Runtime API Usage whitelists whether the running app can call Oracle APEX's own admin APIs to modify itself, other apps, or workspace users; Pass ECID forwards a distributed-tracing ID on outbound REST calls for end-to-end correlation.
workflow: Enable Modify This Application only if a page process legitimately needs to flip its own build options at runtime via API.
skip_for_web: Both are Oracle-APEX-platform self-modification/tracing concepts; a JS app's equivalent of Pass ECID is a trace/correlation-id header, which OpenTelemetry-style tooling already provides.

name: Security: Authentication (app-level)
apex: Identifies which one Authentication Scheme is current for the app, and the Public User schema name whose sessions count as anonymous (APP_USER equals it) for conditional public/private display.
workflow: Pick the app's current auth scheme here; compare APP_USER to Public User to show a login button vs a logout link.
skip_for_web: Paddock uses Clerk for authentication, so APEX's Authentication Scheme picker and Public User substitution do not apply; Clerk's client SDK provides the equivalent signed-in/anonymous check.

name: Security: Authorization (app-level)
apex: One authorization scheme can be required app-wide, checked on every page; Run on Public Pages decides if it also applies to pages that don't otherwise require login; Source for Role/Group Schemes says where Is-In-Role/Group checks look.
attributes: Source for Role or Group Schemes
workflow: Set an app-level Authorization Scheme only when every page needs the same gate; otherwise attach schemes per-page or per-component instead.

name: Security: Browser Security
apex: Standard browser-facing hardening: disable page caching so a logged-out user can't back-button into cached sensitive pages, control frame-embedding to block clickjacking, choose how special characters are HTML-escaped, and add custom security headers.
attributes: Embed in Frames (Deny/Allow from same origin/Allow)
workflow: Disable Cache and set Embed in Frames to Deny or same-origin as a baseline; add extra HTTP Response Headers for anything APEX doesn't set itself.

name: Security: Database Session
apex: Low-level DB session hooks: which schema parses the app's SQL, a PL/SQL block run at the very start of each page request and one at the end for cleanup, plus which Oracle APEX admin APIs the running app may call on itself or others.
workflow: Use Initialization PL/SQL Code to set a session variable from APP_USER at the start of every request.
skip_for_web: Parsing Schema and Initialization/Cleanup PL/SQL blocks are Oracle-database session mechanics with no direct JS-app equivalent.

name: Security: Session Management
apex: Controls session lifetime and rejoin behavior: whether a URL lacking a session ID may reuse an existing browser-cookie session, whether deep links land where they say, and timeouts for total session length vs idle time, each with its own redirect URL and warning.
attributes: Maximum Session Idle Time in Seconds
workflow: Set Maximum Session Idle Time plus a Session Idle Timeout URL so an abandoned tab logs out cleanly instead of leaving state open.
skip_for_web: Rejoin Sessions and Session State Commits are APEX's own server-session model; a JS app's session lives in a signed cookie/JWT (e.g. Clerk) with its own expiry config.

name: Security: Session State Protection
apex: Anti-URL-tampering: APEX appends a checksum to bookmarkable URLs so item values in the link can't be forged; Expire Bookmarks rotates the checksum salt to invalidate every old bookmarked link at once.
workflow: Turn on Session State Protection app-wide, then set per-item protection levels; click Expire Bookmarks if a checksum salt may have leaked.
skip_for_web: URL-embedded checksums are specific to APEX's f?p= URL scheme; a JS app validates request params server-side per request instead.

name: Application Setting
apex: A named app-level config value (like an env var) developers read at runtime via APEX_APP_SETTING; has a default Value, an optional comma-separated whitelist of Valid Values, and an On Upgrade Keep Value flag.
workflow: Create Setting once, read its value from PL/SQL via APEX_APP_SETTING; a deployed environment can change the value via APEX_APP_SETTING.SET_VALUE and On Upgrade Keep Value stops the next deploy from overwriting it.

name: Application Setting vs Build Option (which to use)
apex: Two different app-wide configuration primitives: an Application Setting stores a VALUE developers read at runtime (e.g. a URL or a page-size limit); a Build Option stores an ON/OFF switch that enables or completely removes a component from the running app.
workflow: Use an Application Setting when the app needs a configurable value; use a Build Option when a whole feature or component should be togglable in or out entirely.

name: Build Option - Selecting & Deleting
apex: A build option is applied by picking it from a page, component, page control, or shared component's Configuration/Build Option property in Page Designer; deleting a build option requires first removing it from every component that references it.
attributes: Build Option (attached at Configuration, Build Option)
workflow: Before deleting a build option, detach it from all referencing components (check the Utilization report) or the delete is blocked.

name: Build Option (component attributes)
apex: The editable record behind a build option: its name, current Status, what Status an export resets it to (Default on Export), and whether upgrading the app preserves a deployed environment's own Status.
workflow: Create the build option in Shared Components, then attach it via any component's Configuration, Build Option property; check Utilization/History reports to see where it is used.

name: Build Option reports & export
apex: Utilization report shows every component a build option is attached to; History shows past status changes; a build option's Status can be exported and toggled per target environment without redeploying the whole app.
workflow: Before deleting a build option, check Utilization first and detach its components, since a build option can't be deleted while still referenced.

name: Build Options (concept)
apex: A named on/off switch attachable to almost any component (pages, regions, items, buttons, validations, list entries); Include ships the component with the app, Exclude makes the engine treat it as if it doesn't exist.
workflow: Use one build option per installation variant or feature flag so a single app codebase ships different feature sets; the built-in 'Commented Out' option powers Page Designer's per-component comment-out toggle.
skip_for_web: Evaluated by the Oracle APEX engine server-side at render time; a JS app gets the same effect from a build-time env flag (tree-shaken out) or a runtime feature-flag check, not a per-component database attribute.

name: Shortcut
apex: A reusable snippet of HTML, an image reference, or a PL/SQL function body defined once and invoked by its Static ID wherever a region source, item label, or template attribute accepts shortcut syntax, cutting down on copy-pasted markup or code.
attributes: Type (Function Body returning VARCHAR2/HTML Text/HTML Text with Escaped Special Chars/Image/Text with JavaScript Escaped Single Quotes/Message/Message with JavaScript Escaped Special Quotes)
workflow: Define a shortcut of the right Type once, then reference it as "SHORTCUT_STATIC_ID" in a Region Source (HTML Text with shortcuts), a Region Header/Footer, or an Item Label/Pre-Post Element Text.
skip_for_web: Function Body Returning VARCHAR2 is server-rendered-string logic specific to APEX; a JS app gets the same 'define once, use everywhere' behavior from a shared component or i18n message instead of a text-substitution snippet.

name: Shortcut Reports & Referencing Locations
apex: A shortcut can only be referenced from specific attribute types: Region Source (HTML Text with shortcuts), Region Header/Footer Text, Item Label/Pre-Post Element Text/Default Value, and Region Template attributes, invoked as "SHORTCUT_STATIC_ID" in quotes.
workflow: Reference a shortcut only in one of its supported attribute locations; check the History tab to see recently changed shortcuts across the app.

name: Text Message
apex: A named, per-language text string called from PL/SQL (APEX_LANG) or JavaScript (APEX.LANG.*) to keep user-facing copy translatable instead of hardcoded; supports named (%name) or positional (%0,%1) substitution placeholders that must match across every language's version.
workflow: Create one Text Message per string, flip Used in JavaScript if called client-side, reference it as &{MESSAGE_NAME}. in templates/PL-SQL or via the JS API; add one row per language for translations.
skip_for_web: APEX_LANG/APEX.LANG.* runtime message lookup by language is APEX's own i18n plumbing; a JS app gets the same from an i18n library's message catalog and its own {name}-style interpolation.

name: Translating Messages workflow
apex: A general multi-step process for shipping an app in several languages using Text Messages: author every string as a base-language message, add translated rows per language, then search/select the right translation message from within Page Designer wherever text is needed.
workflow: Write UI copy as Text Messages from day one (even for a single-language app) so adding a second language later means adding rows, not rewriting pages.

name: Calling a JavaScript file from the Page Template
apex: A page template can reference a .js file directly, so every page using that template loads that script automatically.
attributes: JS file reference in page template markup
workflow: Add a <script src> style reference inside the page template's HTML so it's included on every page built from it.

name: Files (theme attribute: File Prefix + Create File)
apex: File Prefix sets the base URL the web server uses for a theme static files; blank means files serve from the database. #THEME_FILES# resolves per File Prefix, #THEME_DB_FILES# always forces the DB-stored copy, #APEX_FILES# points at APEX own file base. Create File uploads a file into the theme.
workflow: Leave File Prefix blank to store/serve theme files from the DB, or point it at a web-server path for performance; use Create File to upload assets such as css/images.
skip_for_web: Choosing between DB-stored theme files and a web-server path is an Oracle-APEX storage concern; a Next.js app just serves static assets from its own hosting/CDN.

name: Referencing an uploaded CSS file (page template Header)
apex: An uploaded stylesheet is wired in by hand-adding a <link> tag inside the Page Template's Header section, using #APP_FILES# to point at an app-scoped upload or #WORKSPACE_FILES# for a workspace-scoped one; loads alongside #TITLE#/#HEAD# in the document head.
workflow: Themes > theme > View Templates > open the page template > add <link rel="stylesheet" href="#APP_FILES#name.css"> inside Header.

name: Static CSS file upload + scope
apex: A CSS file can be uploaded as a Static Application File (scoped to one app) or a Static Workspace File (scoped to every app in the workspace), independent of the theme-file mechanism, for ad hoc custom styling.
workflow: Upload once, then reference it from a template rather than pasting CSS inline.
skip_for_web: Workspace-scoped file sharing across multiple apps only matters in Oracle's multi-app workspace model.

name: Theme CSS/image file locations
apex: Each built-in theme ships its own CSS and images under /i/themes/theme_xx (and /css, /images subfolders); filenames embed the APEX version number for backward compatibility with older imported apps.
workflow: Templates reference their theme's CSS; the CSS/images are versioned per theme so old exported apps keep rendering correctly after an APEX upgrade.
skip_for_web: Version-suffixed CSS paths solve cross-version app import compatibility, not relevant to a single continuously-deployed web app.

name: Theme-level JavaScript File URLs / CSS File URLs
apex: Lists of external JS/CSS URLs, one per line, loaded on every page of the app; they substitute into the page template at #THEME_JAVASCRIPT# and #THEME_CSS# respectively.
workflow: List asset URLs on the theme; debug mode auto-swaps minified vs unminified via #MIN#/#MIN_DIRECTORY#; page template must contain the matching placeholder to render them.
skip_for_web: The #MIN#/#MIN_DIRECTORY# debug-mode auto-swap is specific to APEX's runtime engine.

name: Application Logo (User Interface Attributes)
apex: The logo shown in the app's top navigation bar at runtime; requires the page template to include the #LOGO# substitution string. Configured under User Interface Attributes > Logo, with a Logo type selector that reveals different fields: None (no logo), Image (Image URL, e.g. #APP_FILES#my-logo.png), Text (plain Text label), Image and Text (both an Image URL and Text), Custom (raw Custom HTML inserted directly into the #LOGO# token).
attributes: Logo type: Image and Text (Image URL + Text)
#APP_FILES# / static file reference in Image URL
workflow: Application home > Edit Application Definition > User Interface tab (or Shared Components > User Interface Attributes) > Logo > pick type > fill its field(s) > Apply Changes.

name: Editing App Logo at Runtime (Edit Logo dialog)
apex: A live shortcut to change the logo without opening Shared Components: Developer toolbar > Customize > Edit Logo opens a dialog with Type None/Text/Image/Image and Text, where Image accepts a drag-and-drop upload (must be under 500 KB). Custom HTML is deliberately excluded here for security; picking it redirects to the full User Interface Attributes page instead.
workflow: Run the page, Customize > Edit Logo, pick Type, fill it in, Save; use the full User Interface Attributes page instead when Custom HTML is needed.

name: Template Component (plug-in type)
apex: A plug-in type for building reusable UI components inside Page Designer, not based on PL/SQL. Built from an HTML template with template directives (special tokens controlling how surrounding text is processed). Renders two ways: standalone as a region (one or many rows), or embedded inside a report as a partial for one column.
attributes: Standalone region rendering (single or multiple rows)
Action Positions / Action Templates (row-level conditional actions and menu buttons)
workflow: Developer builds the plug-in's HTML template with directives once; any region or report column can then use it, editing its exposed attributes in Page Designer like any other plug-in.
skip_for_web: The plug-in-not-PL/SQL framing and Page Designer registration model are Oracle APEX's own extension mechanism.

name: Template Component region capabilities
apex: Regions built on a Template Component plug-in get built-in report-like behavior for free: instant single/multi-row display, remembered pagination, faceted search and smart filters, external Order By support, single/multi row selection with keyboard navigation, and grouping of report data.
workflow: Pick a Template Component as the region's type to inherit these interaction behaviors without coding them.

name: Creating / Editing a Template Option Group
apex: A named grouping of related template options scoped to one Template Type, configured via the Template Options Groups window opened from a template's Template Options section.
attributes: Null Text (shown when the user picks none)
workflow: On a template: Template Options > Template Options Groups > Add Template Option Group; set Template Type/Name/Identifier/Null Text/Advanced; Save. Delete via Row Actions > Delete Row.

name: Creating a Template Option
apex: A row added under a template's Template Options list (Shared Components > Templates > pick template > Add Template Option) that maps a name to one or more CSS classes, optionally inside a Group.
attributes: Identifier (uppercase, alphanumeric, immutable, used for cross-theme mapping)
workflow: Pick the template, Add Template Option, fill Group/Name/Identifier/Classes/Help Text/Static ID, Save. Requires being the theme owner (not just a subscriber).

name: Default Template Option / #DEFAULT#
apex: A template-level default option not tied to a group; App Builder applies it at render time via a #DEFAULT# substitution string rather than writing it into the component, so changing the template's default updates every component using it centrally. A developer can turn off the default per component to hand-pick options instead.
workflow: Leave a component on #DEFAULT# to inherit whatever the template's default option is; disable it and pick specific options when a component needs to diverge, which then get written into that component's own CSS-classes metadata.

name: Editing / Deleting a Template Option
apex: Same attribute set as creation, edited inline on the Templates page's Template Options grid; renaming the Classes value requires manually updating every component that already referenced the old class name, and Identifier can never be changed once set (it drives theme-switch mapping). Deletion is via the grid's Row Actions menu.
workflow: Select the option's row on the Templates page, edit fields, Save; deleting uses Row Actions > Delete Row. Global Template Options are visible by expanding a separate section.

name: Global Template Option
apex: A template option defined on the Themes page (theme-level) rather than on one specific template, and therefore available to every component of the chosen Template Type across the whole theme, not just components using one template. Same attribute shape as a per-template option but adds a Template Type selector.
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > pick theme > Template Options > Add Template Option; pick Template Type first, then fill the rest; requires theme-owner rights. Edit/delete on the same grid (Row Actions > Delete Row); renaming Classes needs manual updates on components already using it.

name: Global Template Option Group
apex: A template option group defined at the theme level (Themes page) instead of on one template, so its Preset and Basic/Advanced classification apply for all components of the group's Template Type theme-wide.
workflow: Themes > pick theme > Template Options > Template Options Groups > Add Template Option Group; fill fields, Save. A preset for the group is still chosen at the individual template level, e.g. a specific button template picks Small as its default from the theme-wide Button Size group.

name: Live Template Options (Quick Edit dialog)
apex: A live, no-refresh way to change a component's template options: from the Developer toolbar's Quick Edit mode, hover a component and click its wrench icon to open the Live Template Options dialog (region-based components like lists/classic reports also get an Attributes tab there).
workflow: Run the page, click Quick Edit, hover the target component, click its wrench icon, change options/attributes, Save — updates render immediately without a full page reload.

name: Template Option
apex: A declarative CSS modifier a developer attaches to a component's chosen template, letting one template render in many visual variants (color, spacing, alignment, with/without icon) instead of needing near-duplicate templates per variant. Supported on pages, regions, classic reports, breadcrumbs, lists, items/labels, and buttons.
attributes: CSS modifier (maps to a CSS class)
workflow: Pick a template once, then flip template options on the component's Appearance settings to vary its look without writing CSS.

name: Template Option Group: Advanced flag (Basic vs Advanced)
apex: A Yes/No setting on a template option group that files it under the Basic or Advanced category of options shown to the developer, letting common choices surface first and niche ones hide behind an Advanced toggle.
workflow: Set Yes to keep a rarely-used option group tucked under an Advanced section rather than cluttering the main options list.

name: Template Option Groups and Presets
apex: A named group collecting related template options (e.g. Button Size, Button Style, Form Label Position). At the template level a developer can set one option in the group as the Preset, which auto-applies to every new component created against that template; group options are otherwise optional unless a preset is set.
attributes: Preset (template-level default choice within a group)
workflow: Define a group (e.g. Button Size: Large/Small) on a template, set Small as the Preset, and every new button on that template starts as Small automatically.

name: Breadcrumb Template
apex: Controls how a hierarchical-navigation breadcrumb region renders, as a link list or a breadcrumb path; chosen when creating a breadcrumb region. Definition has Before First (opening HTML, must carry #COMPONENT_CSS_CLASSES# if Template Options exist), Current Page Breadcrumb Entry, Non Current Page Breadcrumb Entry, After Last (closing HTML), Between Level (separator), and Maximum Levels (how many levels display).
workflow: Style the current-page crumb differently from the rest; cap depth with Maximum Levels for deep page hierarchies.

name: Breadcrumb Template: substitution strings
apex: Current Entry and Non Current Entry HTML both accept the same token set to render one crumb: #LINK# (URL), #NAME# (label), #LONG_NAME# (fuller label), #NAME_ESC_SC# (HTML-escaped label).

name: Button Template
apex: Optional template customizing a button's look via multiple images or HTML tags. Same Name-section pattern as other templates (Template Class for theme-switch mapping, Translatable). Definition holds two variants: Normal Template (rendered for Normal-type buttons) and Hot Template (rendered for Hot-type buttons), each its own HTML with substitution strings.
workflow: Leave unset to use the theme default button rendering; define Normal/Hot Template HTML to give buttons of each type custom markup.

name: Button Template: substitution strings
apex: The same token set is valid in both Normal and Hot Template HTML: button attributes/CSS classes/DOM id/name/icon classes/label/link/click handling. #BUTTON_CSS_CLASSES# specifically must be included whenever the template has Template Options defined, since that is where the chosen option's CSS classes get injected at runtime.
workflow: Always include #BUTTON_CSS_CLASSES# in a button template that defines Template Options, or the chosen option's class never reaches the rendered button.

name: Creating a New Template (procedure)
apex: Templates page > Create; pick the template Type, then a creation method, From Scratch or As a Copy of an Existing Template; must associate the new template with the correct theme.
attributes: As a Copy of an Existing Template
workflow: Shared Components > Templates > Create > choose Type > choose From Scratch or Copy > follow wizard, confirming the target theme.

name: Custom template workflow (general)
apex: Oracle recommends never building a template from a blank slate: start from an existing template in the theme and modify it, since the APEX engine already builds the whole UI from named theme templates.
workflow: Duplicate a close-fitting template, then edit its markup/options rather than authoring one from scratch.

name: Default Page Template selection
apex: A theme has one default page template applied to new pages; a developer can override it per-page. Selecting the theme-wide default vs a page-specific template are two different settings.
workflow: Set the theme's default once; override on individual pages that need a different layout (e.g. a login page or a modal page).

name: Escaping syntax in substitution strings
apex: A syntax for escaping template #SUBSTITUTION# placeholders so they can be output literally instead of being replaced, when a template's markup needs to contain a literal hash-delimited token.
workflow: Used when authoring template markup that must show a literal '#TOKEN#'-shaped string rather than trigger substitution.

name: Generic Column Template vs Named Column Template
apex: Generic defines one column's look once (e.g. #COLUMN_VALUE#), repeated for however many columns the report has; limited to standard row/column reports, styled further only via conditions. Named references specific column names directly in the row's HTML, giving more layout freedom but tying the template to one query shape (expression columns need a SQL alias to avoid errors).
attributes: Named: per-column tokens in one row layout
workflow: Use Named when columns need very different layouts (e.g. a card-style row mixing text and image columns) rather than a uniform grid.

name: Label Templates
apex: Templates that centrally manage the HTML markup used to render page item labels, so label markup/styling is controlled in one place instead of per item.
attributes: Label template markup (referenced by page items)
workflow: Assign a label template to items; edit the template once to restyle every label using it.

name: List Template / Hierarchical Lists
apex: Controls how a shared list of links renders. A list can be hierarchical (nested sublists) only if built on a list template named with the convention "with Sublist", and each entry then picks a Parent List Entry to nest under.
attributes: Template naming convention "with Sublist" (marks hierarchy support)
Parent List Entry (set per list entry)
workflow: Pick a "with Sublist" template when the list needs nesting; otherwise any list template works for a flat list.

name: List Template: Sublist Entry and substitution strings
apex: Before/After Sublist Entry wrap the nested sublist block; Sublist Entry mirrors the top-level Current/Noncurrent (+with-sub-list-items) pattern for nested items plus Between Sub List Items separator. Common tokens across list templates: #LINK#, #TEXT#, #TEXT_ESC_SC#, #ICON_CSS_CLASSES#, #IMAGE#, #IMAGE_ATTR#, #APEX_FILES#, #A01#-#A10# (custom attribute slots), #LIST_ITEM_ID#, #PARENT_LIST_ITEM_ID#.
attributes: Sub List Template Current / Noncurrent (+ with sublist items)
workflow: Mirror the top-level entry design one level down for nested items; #A01#-#A10# let a list entry carry extra custom values into the template.

name: List Template: wrapper and per-entry HTML
apex: Before List Entry / After List Entry open and close a wrapper around the whole list (e.g. an HTML table); must include #COMPONENT_CSS_CLASSES# in Before List Entry if the template has Template Options. Template Definition supplies Current vs Noncurrent entry HTML (each with a with-sublist-items variant) plus Between List Elements separator HTML; Template Definitions for First Entry lets the first list item override any of those four variants.
attributes: Before List Entry (#COMPONENT_CSS_CLASSES# required if options exist)
List Template Current with Sub List Items
List Template Noncurrent with Sub List Items
workflow: Set Before/After List Entry once for the outer wrapper; Current vs Noncurrent HTML distinguishes the selected nav entry from the rest; override the First variant only when item 1 needs different markup.

name: Page Template
apex: Defines a page's overall layout: a Header, Body, Footer and several subtemplates, built from static HTML plus UPPERCASE #SUBSTITUTION# placeholders marking where dynamic content/components go. If a page doesn't pick one explicitly, APEX uses the theme's default page template.
workflow: Assign a page template per page (or rely on the theme default); edit its Header/Body/Footer HTML to change every page using it at once.

name: Page Template: Definition (Header/Body/Footer)
apex: The three HTML blocks that make up the template. Header builds the document <head> (should include #TITLE# and #HEAD#); Body builds the <body>, with substitution strings marking where main content and additional region positions sit; Footer is HTML rendered after the Body.
workflow: Write the page shell once here; every region's Display Point placeholder in Body determines where that region can be placed.

name: Page Template: Dialog attributes (template-level + required)
apex: Only shown/required when Template Type is Dialog Page: Width, Height, Maximum Width, extra CSS Classes, and Allow Embed in Frames (governs iframe embedding of modal dialogs, interacting with the app's Browser Frame security setting). All are page-template-level defaults that an individual page can override.
workflow: Set sensible dialog-size defaults on the Dialog Page template; override per-page only when one dialog needs a different size.

name: Page Template: JavaScript and CSS attributes
apex: Per-page-template script/style loading and inline code. JS File URLs and CSS File URLs load per-page assets (support #MIN#/#MIN_DIRECTORY#/#APP_VERSION#); Function and Global Variable Declaration and inline CSS replace #TEMPLATE_JAVASCRIPT#/#TEMPLATE_CSS#; Execute when Page Loads runs after APEX's own generated JS (#GENERATED_JAVASCRIPT#); Dialog Initialization/Closure/Cancel Code (Dialog Page type only) wire up dialog behavior in JS.
workflow: Put reusable script/style in File URLs (cacheable, external); put page-shell-specific code inline; Dialog-only fields appear only when Template Type is Dialog Page.

name: Page Template: Layout types and Positions
apex: Layout Type picks how regions/items/buttons are positioned: HTML Table (table-based), Fixed Number of Columns (a fixed grid column count), or Variable Number of Columns (grid columns grow with content). Positions are developer-named placement slots (display points) a component can target; a position's name can't collide with a reserved page substitution string (e.g. NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE).
attributes: Layout Type: Fixed Number of Columns
Layout Type: Variable Number of Columns
workflow: Pick a Layout Type for the template's grid model, then define named Positions so regions/items/buttons have a place to be assigned on pages using this template.

name: Page Template: Name section
apex: Identity fields: Template Class (used to map this template to an equivalent one when switching themes), a Translatable checkbox (flags the template as containing user-facing text needing translation), and Template Type, Normal Page or Dialog Page, which restricts the template to pages of matching page mode.
workflow: Set Template Type to Dialog Page to make the template selectable only for Modal/Non-Modal pages; Normal Page templates only apply to Normal-mode pages.

name: Page Template: Subtemplates and Image-Based Tab Attributes
apex: HTML snippets substituted into the Header/Body/Footer at named tokens: Success Message (#SUCCESS_MESSAGE#), Navigation Bar (#NAVIGATION_BAR#, with #BAR_BODY# marking where entries go) plus a per-entry Navigation Bar Entry snippet, and Notification (#NOTIFICATION_MESSAGE#). Image Based Tab Attributes supply Current Image Tab and Non Current Image Tab HTML (using #TAB_TEXT#) for image-only tab styling.
workflow: Fill these only if the template needs custom markup for that piece; unset ones fall back to nothing rendered at that token.

name: Popup LOV Templates
apex: Templates controlling how the popup list-of-values dialog displays for every page item defined with a POPUP-type LOV.
workflow: Assign to items using a popup LOV; one template governs the popup's appearance app-wide.

name: Region Display Point / Position utilization
apex: Regions are placed on a page by Display Point (position); which display points exist is determined entirely by the page's assigned page-level template. A report (Task list > View page template region position utilization) shows usage across the app.
attributes: Display Point (region position, defined by page template)
workflow: Check the page template to see what display points/positions are available before placing a region; use the utilization report to audit usage app-wide.

name: Region Template
apex: Controls the appearance and placement of a region's content. Built from HTML wrapping the region plus UPPERCASE #SUBSTITUTION# strings; #BODY# is the only required one and marks where the region's own content goes, everything else is optional.
workflow: Write wrapper HTML around #BODY#; add optional reserved tokens (title, header/footer, image) or custom Positions for extra slots like sub-regions.

name: Region Template: Image sub-template
apex: Defines extra HTML around a region's image. #REGION_IMAGE_URL# is required (used as an src); #REGION_IMAGE_ALT_TEXT# and #REGION_IMAGE_ATTRIBUTES# are optional; its output is placed into the main region template via #REGION_IMAGE#.
workflow: Fill in when a region type displays an image (e.g. a card-style region) and needs custom markup around it.

name: Region Template: JavaScript and CSS attributes
apex: Same shape as page templates but scoped to the region: JS/CSS File URLs (support #MIN#/#MIN_DIRECTORY#/#APP_VERSION#) load assets used by that region, and Execute when Page Loads runs region-specific JS after APEX's own generated script.
workflow: Attach assets/behavior only needed when this region template is used, instead of loading them app-wide.

name: Region Template: Name section
apex: Same identity pattern as page templates: Theme membership, Name, a Template Class used to map this template to an equivalent one on theme switch, and a Translatable checkbox for templates containing user-facing text.

name: Region Template: Positions (region position slots)
apex: A Positions section on the region template defines named slots (display points) inside the region besides #BODY#, such as #SUB_REGIONS#, where other components can be placed. Layout additionally exposes HTML-table attributes for page items placed in the region, only relevant when the page template's own layout Type is HTML Table (not a fixed/variable grid).
attributes: Layout: HTML table attributes for items (HTML Table layout only)
workflow: Add a custom Position when the region needs another content slot beyond its main body (e.g. a side panel); items only get HTML-table layout attributes when the page uses table-based layout.

name: Region Template: reserved substitution strings
apex: Tokens the region engine fills from Page Designer's region settings: title/paging tokens, form open/close, IDs, CSS classes/attributes, header/footer HTML, and the region-image group. Used anywhere in the region template's HTML.
workflow: Place whichever tokens the template's design needs; APEX substitutes each with the region's actual configured value at render time.

name: Region Template: Sub Regions sub-templates
apex: Three linked sub-templates build a titled list of a region's sub-regions: Header Template wraps the whole list (#ENTRIES# required, placed via #SUB_REGION_HEADERS# in the main region template); Header Entry Template renders one title per sub-region (#SUB_REGION_ID#, #SUB_REGION_TITLE#, placed via #ENTRIES#); Template wraps each actual sub-region's content (#SUB_REGION# required, placed via #SUB_REGIONS#).
workflow: Use when a region contains nested sub-regions (e.g. a tabbed or accordion container) and each needs both a title-list entry and its own content wrapper.

name: Replace All Templates within an Application
apex: Bulk-imports another application's whole template set into the current app, mapping each component to a New Template chosen per component, either by Replace (copy the definition) or Replace/Subscribe (copy plus create a live subscription back to the source).
workflow: Use to re-skin an app wholesale from a sibling app's theme/templates, optionally keeping them linked via subscription for future updates.
skip_for_web: Cross-application template borrowing assumes an Oracle multi-app workspace; a single web app has one template set.

name: Replace Templates wizard
apex: Bulk-swaps the template assigned to components of one Template Type: pick the type, then Change From one template to Change To another; every matching component gets reassigned.
workflow: Templates page > Task list > Replace Templates > pick type > choose From/To > Finish.

name: Report (Column) Template
apex: Controls one cell/column's rendering from a SQL query row, not the whole row by itself (wrapper sections handle the row/table shell separately). Columns are addressed positionally (#1#, #2#, #3#...) or, in Named Column Templates, by column name (#ENAME#); app items are referenced with &ITEM_NAME. syntax. Two flavors exist: Generic Column Templates and Named Column Templates.
workflow: Pick Generic for a standard uniform row/column report; pick Named when you need column-specific markup and don't mind rebuilding the template per query shape.

name: Report Template: Before Rows / After Rows / Pagination wrapper
apex: Before Rows is HTML rendered once before any row (typically opens a <table>; can include #TOP_PAGINATION# for a top pager, #CSV_LINK# for a CSV export link, #REPORT_ATTRIBUTES# set per report region). After Rows closes the wrapper and supports #PAGINATION#, #COLCOUNT#, #CSV_LINK#, #EXTERNAL_LINK# (e.g. a PDF export link). Pagination Subtemplate defines the Pagination Template shell (#TEXT#) plus Next Page/Previous Page/Next Set/Previous Set link templates (#LINK#).
workflow: Open/close the report's outer table shell in Before/After Rows; style pager links independently in the Pagination Subtemplate section.

name: Report Template: Column Headings, Row Highlighting, Subscription
apex: Column Headings has Before/Column Heading Template (colorizes the header cell, or OMIT to hide headings, else a default applies)/After. Row Highlighting sets background colors for a checked row and for the current (hovered) row. Named Column Templates additionally have a Subscription section: pick an existing template to subscribe to (become a read-only follower of a master), with Refresh to pull the latest master copy.
workflow: Use OMIT to suppress column headers entirely; use Subscription to keep a report template in sync with a shared master definition.
skip_for_web: Template subscription/master-refresh is Oracle's own reuse mechanism.

name: Report Template: Column/Row Templates (conditional styling)
apex: Up to four Column Templates (Generic) or Row Templates (Named), each optionally conditional via a Column Template Condition: Use Based on PL/SQL Expression (row-data-driven), Use for Even Numbered Rows, or Use for Odd Numbered Rows — letting a report alternate or conditionally style rows without JavaScript. Shared tokens: #ALIGNMENT#, #COLCOUNT#, #COLNUM#, #COLUMN_HEADER#, #COLUMN_VALUE#, #ROWNUM#.
workflow: Define one Column/Row Template per visual variant needed (e.g. default + over-threshold highlight), each guarded by its own condition; APEX picks the first matching one per row/column at render time.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL-expression row conditions are Oracle-SQL-specific; a JS/TS app would express the same conditional styling in its own render logic.

name: Template Reports (utilization/subscription/publish/history)
apex: Built-in reports describing how templates are used across an app: which components use which template, subscription status, published templates, and edit history.
workflow: Developer opens these reports to audit template usage before changing or deleting a shared template.

name: Template Subscription: Unsubscribe / Publish
apex: A subscribed template's definition is maintained by a separate referenced (master) template. Unsubscribe Templates breaks that link for a chosen template type in a theme. Publish Templates (Publish tab) pushes the current master template's content out to everything still subscribed to it.
attributes: Unsubscribe Templates page (by theme + template type)
workflow: Master-template owner edits once, then Publish Checked to push the change to all subscribers; a subscriber can Unsubscribe to make its copy independently editable.
skip_for_web: Master/subscriber template propagation is Oracle's multi-app content-sharing model.

name: Templates page (Shared Components)
apex: The central list of all templates in the app (Shared Components > User Interface > Templates); clicking a template name opens its definition for editing. A Return to Page checkbox lets a developer keep a specific running page current while editing the template in another window.
workflow: Open a template from the list, edit attributes/markup, Apply Changes; check Return to Page to immediately re-view the effect on the page you were editing.

name: apex.utr.config() developer-console API
apex: A JavaScript function exposed in the browser console that reads or writes Theme Roller's live configuration (classes, vars, customCSS, useCustomLess) directly, without opening the Theme Roller dialog UI.
attributes: apex.utr.config() with no args (read current config)
workflow: Call with no args to dump current Theme Roller state as JSON; call with a JSON object (e.g. custom CSS in customCSS) to push it live, then it appears in Theme Roller's own Code Editor.
skip_for_web: A console-exposed live-config API is an APEX developer-tooling convenience; a web app edits its own CSS files/state directly.

name: Creating a Theme Style
apex: Add Style on the theme's Styles tab creates a new named style, cloned conceptually from an existing one, with its own settings, visibility, and Theme Roller linkage.
workflow: Themes > pick theme > Styles tab > Add Style > fill Settings + Theme Roller Attributes > Create.

name: Editing / Deleting a Theme Style
apex: On the theme's Styles tab, clicking a style name opens its attributes to edit (Apply Changes) or remove (Delete); the tab also shows/changes the Current Theme Style.
workflow: Shared Components > Themes > theme Name > Styles tab > click a style Name to edit or delete it, or switch which style is current.

name: Enable End Users to choose Theme Style
apex: A User Interface Attributes toggle that, once on, shows a Customize link (typically bottom-left) in the running app; clicking it lets the end user pick among the theme's styles, and the choice persists as that user's own preference across sessions.
attributes: Enable End Users to choose Theme Style (toggle)
workflow: Requires 2+ theme styles on the app; turn the toggle on so real users, not just developers, can self-select a look (e.g. light/dark).

name: Import / Export Theme Styles (Theme Roller)
apex: Theme Roller's Additional Options menu can export the current style's configuration to a JSON file, or import one, using a fixed JSON shape: classes (array), vars (object of variable values), customCSS (string), useCustomLess ("Y"/"N").
attributes: JSON keys: classes, vars, customCSS, useCustomLess
workflow: Export a finished style's JSON to move/back it up; Import applies a JSON file's classes/vars/customCSS/useCustomLess onto the current style.

name: Redwood Light: Pillar / Layout / Appearance classes
apex: The Redwood Light theme style exposes extra Theme Roller class-based options beyond colors: Pillar swaps background/header images, Layout switches page width mode (Edge to Edge, Floating, Contained), and Appearance groups Header, Navigation, Body Header and Background controls.
workflow: Pick a Layout mode to control whether the page content spans full width, floats with margins, or sits in a fixed contained width; use Pillar/Appearance to swap imagery and section coloring.

name: Reset a Theme Style (Theme Roller)
apex: Additional Options menu item next to Save As that discards unsaved Theme Roller edits and reverts the style to its last-saved state.
workflow: Use to bail out of an in-progress edit without saving.

name: Selecting a Theme Style (User Interface Attributes page)
apex: The app-level User Interface Attributes page has a Theme Style setting the developer changes to switch which style is active app-wide.
attributes: User Interface Attributes page: Theme Style
workflow: Shared Components > User Interface Attributes > Attributes > Theme Style > pick new style > Apply Changes.

name: Styles (theme attribute section)
apex: Lists the Theme Styles available to this theme and shows which one is the Current Theme Style; the active style CSS loads via the #THEME_STYLE_CSS# placeholder in the page template.
workflow: Developer picks the active style here; page template must include #THEME_STYLE_CSS# for it to apply.

name: Theme Roller
apex: A live CSS editor reached from Customize on the Developer toolbar of a running app page. Lets a developer change theme style, colors, rounded corners, and other visual attributes with no code, then Save/Save As back onto a theme style. Requires theme styles to exist with Input Parameter File URLs set.
workflow: Run a page, open Developer toolbar > Customize > Theme Roller; adjust sliders/colors live, then Save (overwrite current style) or Save As (new style, becomes current).

name: Theme Roller / Live Template Options / Logo Editor: mutual exclusion
apex: These three live, in-browser visual editors cannot be used at the same time in one session; only one should be open at once.
workflow: Close one live editor before opening another.

name: Theme Roller Style Compatibility (Iris/Vita/Redwood Light)
apex: Vita-based styles (including the high-contrast Iris style) share one variable set and can exchange Theme Roller JSON exports with each other; Redwood Light uses a different variable set entirely, so importing across the Vita/Redwood Light boundary silently applies no changes.
workflow: Only copy/import Theme Roller exports between styles built on the same base variable set.

name: Theme Roller: Custom CSS box + LESS
apex: A code editor inside Theme Roller where a developer types raw CSS, or LESS if Enable LESS Compilation is switched on; this is layered into the compiled style output alongside the slider-driven variables.
workflow: Use for tweaks the sliders/pickers don't expose; toggle LESS on to use LESS syntax (variables, nesting) instead of plain CSS.
skip_for_web: LESS compilation toggle is specific to Theme Roller's own LESS-based build pipeline.

name: Theme Roller: out-of-the-box themes are locked
apex: Built-in shipped themes/styles cannot be overwritten directly in Theme Roller; a developer must Save As a new theme style first, then modify that copy.
workflow: Edit a shipped style in Theme Roller, then Save As to fork it rather than overwrite the original.

name: Theme Style
apex: A CSS style sheet layered on top of a theme's base CSS to change look and feel (color scheme, flat look, etc.) without touching page templates. Loaded via #THEME_STYLE_CSS# in the page template; a theme can hold several styles with exactly one marked current/active; editable live via Theme Roller.
workflow: Developer keeps several styles per theme (e.g. light/dark or brand variants) and flips which one is active without editing markup.

name: Theme Style: File URLs / CSS Classes
apex: File URLs are the CSS file(s) loaded when this style is current, substituted into #THEME_STYLE_CSS# (supports #MIN#, #MIN_DIRECTORY#, #APP_VERSION#). CSS Classes are extra class names appended to #PAGE_CSS_CLASSES# on every page while this style is active.
workflow: Point File URLs at the style's compiled CSS; add CSS Classes to trigger style-specific selectors elsewhere on the page.

name: Theme Style: Is Public / Accessibility Tested
apex: Is Public controls whether end users are allowed to pick this style from the runtime style picker. Accessibility Tested is a flag recording whether the style has been checked against accessibility guidelines (Oracle documents its own via a VPAT).
workflow: Mark internal/WIP styles not-public so only developers see them; mark a style Accessibility Tested once verified.

name: Theme Style: Theme Roller Attributes (Read Only / LESS / JSON)
apex: Read Only blocks Theme Roller from overwriting the style. Input Parameter File URLs are the LESS source files Theme Roller compiles from; Output CSS File URL is where the compiled CSS is written; the JSON Configuration is Theme Roller's own saved slider/color state (Oracle advises against hand-editing it, though it can be copied from another theme style).
workflow: Theme Roller reads the LESS inputs, lets a developer tweak colors/sliders visually, then writes the compiled CSS to Output CSS File URL and stores slider state as JSON Configuration; set Read Only On to freeze a finished style.
skip_for_web: LESS-based compile-on-save pipeline is Theme Roller's own build step; a hand-coded design system would just edit CSS/CSS variables directly.

name: Component Defaults (theme attribute)
apex: Per-theme default template assigned to each component kind; used automatically whenever a developer creates that kind of component without explicitly picking a template.
attributes: Navigation Bar List / Menu List (Top, Side, Position)
workflow: Set once per theme; every new component of that kind starts on the default template unless the developer overrides it on the component itself.

name: Dialog Defaults (theme attribute)
apex: Per-theme default templates used for modal/non-modal dialog pages created via the Create Page/Application wizards: the dialog shell, its content region, and its button region.
workflow: Wizard-created dialogs pick these templates automatically; Dialog Page also covers separate-page error display.

name: Editing a Theme (procedure)
apex: Shared Components > User Interface > Themes; the Themes page report view shows an Is Current checkmark; clicking a theme name opens Create/Edit Theme with attribute sections to change, saved via Apply Changes.
workflow: App Builder > app > Shared Components > Themes > click theme name > edit attribute sections > Apply Changes.

name: Icons (theme attribute)
apex: Configures the icon set loaded app-wide: which built-in icon Library loads, extra custom icon CSS files/classes offered in the Page Designer icon pickers, a runtime prefix class for non-library icon classes, and the date-picker calendar icon image/attributes.
workflow: Pick a Library for the built-in set; add Custom Library File URLs/Custom Classes to extend the Region/Button icon picker with your own icon font or classes.

name: Migrate to Universal Theme
apex: A migration path to move an application built on an older/non-Universal theme onto the current Universal Theme so it keeps getting features, fixes, and new-component styling.
workflow: Developer runs the documented migration path rather than refresh when the app isn't already on Universal Theme.
skip_for_web: Legacy-theme migration is only relevant because Oracle ships multiple historical themes; a from-scratch web app has one design system.

name: Public Theme (instance-level)
apex: An instance administrator can publish a theme to Oracle APEX Administration Services so it is available to all developers across all workspaces on that instance.
workflow: Admin adds a theme once; all workspace developers can then subscribe/use it.
skip_for_web: PL/SQL/Oracle instance-administration concept; a single-tenant Next.js app has no multi-workspace instance to publish themes to.

name: Refresh Theme
apex: An in-place update of an app's Universal Theme copy to the latest shipped version, picking up new features, bug fixes, and styling for newer APEX components without changing theme identity.
attributes: Refresh Theme button (App Builder home banner)
workflow: App Builder home shows a banner when a newer Universal Theme exists; developer backs up (export/copy) then clicks Refresh Theme, then retests.
skip_for_web: Versioned theme-refresh mechanism is specific to APEX's shipped-theme update model; a web app's CSS is just edited/deployed directly.

name: Region Defaults (theme attribute)
apex: Per-theme default region template used for specific region-content kinds when a developer creates one without explicitly choosing a template.
workflow: Creating e.g. a new Chart region picks up the theme Charts default template automatically.

name: Switch Theme Wizard
apex: Wizard that migrates an app from its current theme to a different installed theme, remapping every component's assigned template to the corresponding template in the new theme by matching template type + class.
workflow: Shared Components > User Interface > Themes > Switch Theme; pick source/target theme, Next to Verify Compatibility, resolve warnings (choose among multiple same-class matches) or errors (no class match), then Switch Theme. Requires 2+ themes installed; back up app first.
skip_for_web: Whole-app template-swap-by-class-matching only matters when multiple interchangeable themes exist; a single hand-built design system has nothing to switch between.

name: Template class mapping (theme switch)
apex: The mechanism App Builder uses to switch themes: every template carries a template type + template class identifier, and switching finds the new theme's template with the same type+class (and name, if multiple match) to substitute.
workflow: If exactly one type+class match exists it's used automatically; multiple matches prompt a manual pick; zero matches of the same class prompts picking a different class (with a functionality-loss warning) or blocks the switch entirely if no template of that type exists at all.

name: Theme
apex: A collection of templates defining the layout and style of an entire application. Templates are organized by template type (page, region, report, list, button, label, popup LOV) then by template class.
workflow: Developer picks/creates a theme; template classes let APEX map templates between themes so switching theme keeps the same UI patterns mapped.

name: Theme Attributes (sections overview)
apex: The Create/Edit Theme page is divided into sections a developer configures per theme: Name, Theme Subscription, JavaScript and CSS, Component Defaults, Region Defaults, Dialog Defaults, Global Template Options, Icons, Styles, Files.
workflow: Developer opens each section on the Create/Edit Theme page to configure that facet of the theme.

name: Theme Attributes: Name section
apex: Identity fields for a theme: its number, developer-facing name, internal identifier, description, plus two structural switches, Navigation Type (Tabs or List) and Navigation Bar Implementation (Classic or List).
workflow: Set once when creating/naming a theme; Navigation Type/Implementation determine which nav UI templates apply.

name: Theme Subscription (theme attribute)
apex: Shows which master theme this app theme subscribes to. Subscribing makes the theme attributes, subscribed template options, and subscribed templates read-only in this app; they must change at the source.
workflow: Point an app theme at a master theme to inherit and lock its definition; edits happen upstream and propagate on refresh.
skip_for_web: Cross-application master-subscription publishing model is an Oracle multi-app-instance feature, not needed by one deployed web app.

name: Universal Theme (Theme 42)
apex: The default APEX theme: responsive design, versatile UI component set, easy customization via Theme Roller and Template Options, and support for Theme Styles (a CSS sheet layered on the base CSS).
workflow: Create Application Wizard uses it by default; developer customizes via Theme Roller + Template Options instead of writing CSS/HTML/JS by hand.
